items.title: Geometric constraints and cognitive inputs jointly shape emergent brain dynamics and topology
items.summary: How the brain's physical geometry gives rise to its flexible functional repertoire remains a central question in neuroscience. Here, we approached this question through recurrent neural networks (RNNs). We trained three RNN classes on a cognitive working-memory task, forming a graded hierarchy of spatial constraints: Vanilla RNNs (no spatial constraints), Masked RNNs (projection constraints limiting where information enters and leaves the network), and biophysical RNNs (bioRNNs; projection constraints and spatial embedding of the networks' connectivity using the brain's inter-regional Euclidean geometry). We assessed how well each RNN class predicted empirical fMRI activity without exposing them to it during training.…

items.title: Same Movements, Different Skills: How Context Shapes Learning in Humans and Neural Networks
items.summary: What determines whether experiences are integrated into shared representations or split? Motor skill learning offers a revealing test: when two tasks require an identical sequence of movements, both intuition and theory suggest that practice in one should generalize to the other. Yet we find that changing context can make identical movements different skills. In simple recurrent networks trained on the same sequence across contexts, splitting was greatest when strong contextual inputs coincided with a high initial weight scale; neither alone sufficed. Greater representational separation coincided with separate context-specific learning curves. Humans practicing the same finger sequence while alternating between two performance-irrelevant contexts likewise exhibited context-specific curves, rather than the single continuous trajectory observed when practicing in a single context.…

items.title: Emergent representations of graphical structure in mechanistic neural models of causal judgment
items.summary: Humans have a remarkable ability to judge causal relationships from a limited number of unreliable observations. Past work on causal cognition has largely focused on normative accounts of human behavior, leaving unknown how biologically plausible neural systems can learn causal relationships from observations and update representations of causal structure with additional evidence. Here, we leverage task-optimized recurrent neural networks to discover candidate implementation-level neural mechanisms of causal judgment. We propose a novel cognitive task in which a subject observes stochastic samples from an unknown causal structure (e.g. among variables A, B, and C with unknown causal relationships), and must judge whether a specific causal relationship is present given a query (e.g. "does A cause C?").…

items.title: Evidence-Gated Plasticity and Context-Dependent Consolidation for Multi-Goal Learning in Spiking Neural Networks
items.summary: Background / Introduction: Biologically inspired spiking neural networks offer a mechanistic framework for adaptive behavior, yet learning multiple goals remains challenging when synaptic updates for different targets interfere. We investigated whether multi-timescale plasticity and context-dependent consolidation improve interleaved multi-goal learning in a spiking navigation system inspired by entorhinal-hippocampal circuitry. Methods: We introduce evidence-gated plasticity (EGP), in which STDP-based reinforcement learning (STDP/RL) generates transient synaptic proposals and need-weighted behavioral evidence modulates their slower consolidation into durable weights. Global EGP pools these proposals and the corresponding evidence across goals.…

items.title: Exponential Map Models as an Interpretable Framework for Generating Neural Spatial Representations
items.summary: A foundational challenge in neuroscience and AI is understanding how physical space is mapped into neural representations. While artificial neural networks can learn brain-like spatial representations, their ``black-box'' nature obscures whether these representations reflect general principles or artifacts of specific architectures, objectives or optimization choices, offering no guarantee that solutions for tasks like path integration generalize beyond training data. Here, we use a first-principles framework based on the matrix exponential, in which generator matrices map physical locations to neural population vectors without gradient-based optimization.…

items.title: Variation in infant subcortical brain development from 6 to 12 months in Down syndrome
items.summary: Introduction: Down syndrome (DS), arising from Trisomy 21, is the most common genetic condition associated with intellectual disability. While smaller total brain volumes have been consistently observed in DS, no longitudinal neuroimaging studies have examined volumetric brain development in DS during infancy, a period of rapid neural growth when interventions may have the greatest impact. Method: High-resolution T1- and T2-weighted images were acquired during natural sleep in a multisite longitudinal cohort of 44 infants with DS and 39 control infants without DS at ages 6 and 12 months. Neuroimaging data were harmonized to reduce batch effects, and a novel deep-learning, repeated-measures segmentation approach was applied to optimize neuroanatomical segmentations.…

items.title: DeePEn - A Depth sensitive benchmark for Protein Engineering
items.summary: Recent progress in modeling techniques and high-throughput screening has significantly enhanced the accessibility of protein engineering. Nevertheless, further progress gets hindered by the lack of robust benchmarks that capture the practical challenges for real-world protein engineering. Here, we introduced DeePEn, a Depth-sensitive benchmark for Protein Engineering that quantifies model generalization to held-out variants at increasing mutational distance from the wild type. We defined distance as the number of simultaneous point mutations, i.e., single amino acid variants (SAVs), moving from wild-type to mutant (edit distance in computer science jargon). DeePEn retrospectively evaluates prediction and prioritization using experimentally labelled variants from deep mutational scanning (DMS) datasets; it does not benchmark prospective sequence generation or goal-directed optimization.…

items.title: Shared Molecular Signatures and Pathways in Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, Schizophrenia, and Bipolar Disorder: An Integrative Transcriptomic and Machine-Learning Study
items.summary: Abstract Objective: Psychiatric disorders such as post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder (BD) are complex conditions with overlapping molecular features that remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify shared molecular abnormalities and potential therapeutic targets associated with these disorders. Methods: RStudio (version 4.4.1) was used to process and analyze gene expression datasets from the NCBI database to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). FunRich, DAVID, STRING, and NetworkAnalyst were used for gene ontology and pathway enrichment, protein-protein interaction analysis, transcription factor and microRNA regulatory network analysis, and protein-chemical interaction analysis. The discriminatory ability of prioritized hub genes and transcription factors was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.…

items.title: Multimodal protein representations across human brain cell types
items.summary: The central nervous system (CNS) comprises diverse cell types whose molecular context shapes the roles of the proteins they express. Computational models offer a scalable way to study the roles of proteins across human brain cell types, with protein language models and interactome- or single-cell-based models capturing complementary information encoded in protein sequences and cellular network contexts. Human brain tissue is hard to access, so brain cell types make up a small fraction of the atlases single-cell models train on and of the benchmarks used for their evaluation.…

items.title: Benchmark Self-Triage (BeST): Comparing Self-Triage Systems and Multiple Generations of OpenAI Models Against Preliminary Expert Consensus
items.summary: As digital self-triage becomes more widely used, quality assurance requires evaluation of both emergency recognition and overall agreement with clinical judgement, including how these outcomes differ across generations of large language models. The Benchmark Self-Triage (BeST) project intends to provide a framework to compare systems for digital self-triage against a medical 'gold standard' in Germany. As a first step in developing and demonstrating the methodology, we compared study-specific implementations of SmED 5.4.11 accessed via API and Infermedica Engine API via Microsoft Azure Healthcare Agent Service with five structured OpenAI configurations spanning multiple model generations: gpt-4.1, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, and gpt-6-astra.…

items.title: Elevated HbA1c is associated with advanced brain age in severe obesity
items.summary: Introduction: Brain-predicted age, estimated from structural MRI data, is a machine-learning biomarker of biological brain aging. Greater brain age gap (BAG) indicates advanced brain aging and is associated with cognitive decline and mortality. Cardiometabolic risk factors, including elevated blood glucose, body mass index (BMI), blood pressure, and cholesterol, increase risk of cognitive impairment and dementia in aging. Their relationship with BAG in severe obesity remains poorly characterized despite increased prevalence of cardiometabolic risk factors among this population. Methods: T1-weighted MRI data from 97 adults (BMI 35-73) were used to calculate BAG using ENIGMA and Pyment brain age models.…

items.title: Silent Drift and Site-level Variance in Clinical AI: Real-world performance and subgroup analysis for post-market monitoring of an FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) triage tool for high-risk use case of pulmonary embolism
items.summary: Background. FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) triage tool for pulmonary embolism (PE) detection has been widely used; however, its performance has not been analyzed for subgroups, clinical sites, and temporal stability. Methods. This retrospective, six-site health system study evaluated the Aidoc BriefCase PE triage model (K190072) across 14,736 CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) examinations between July 2023 and March 2026. Reference-standard PE characteristic labels were extracted from radiology reports using a zero-shot LLM pipeline validated against a radiologist-annotated 600 reports ({kappa} =0.98). Model performance was evaluated across demographics, embolus characteristics, and site. Temporal behavior was evaluated on operating point by logistic regression, with and without site adjustment, and by segmented regression. Results.…

items.title: Automating postmarketing pharmacovigilance with large language model agents
items.summary: Postmarketing pharmacovigilance relies on spontaneous adverse event reporting and labor-intensive observational studies, which suffer from underreporting and delayed risk detection. Large language model (LLM) agents could automate real-world evidence generation, but generalist agents make ad hoc analytical decisions that compromise epidemiological validity and reproducibility. Here we present MedCheckpoint, a multi-agent LLM system for automated postmarketing pharmacovigilance. MedCheckpoint grounds each analytical stage in a curated, source-traceable medical knowledge base, locks core study-design parameters before execution, performs patient-level analyses with human-written deterministic statistical tools, and enforces checkpoint rules that abort infeasible analyses, with optional human-in-the-loop review.…

items.title: Cytokine Signatures of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis and the Modifying Role of Clonal Hematopoiesis: A Machine-Learning and Multi-Omics Study
items.summary: Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) myocarditis affects up to 2% of patients on ICI and has up to a 50% mortality. Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) is a risk factor for ICI myocarditis. Objectives: To leverage a multi-omics approach to evaluate cytokines associated with ICI myocarditis, immunosuppression resistance, CHIP in ICI myocarditis and implicated pathways and cell type contributions. Methods 236 cardio-oncology patients were enrolled, including 88 who were on ICI. Cytokine profiling from patients on ICI were sampled and analyzed using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence. Single-cell multi-omics of peripheral blood from Yale (n=19), Stanford (n=25), and MGH (n=63) evaluated cell-type contributions of cytokines and implicated pathways. Validation of Yale proteomic analyses was done using the Stanford CYTOF dataset.…

items.title: Expert-level localization of fine-grained cardiac structures across the transthoracic echocardiogram
items.summary: Artificial intelligence models for echocardiography interpret studies without identifying the structures that support their outputs. We show that this spatial grounding does not emerge from the pretraining of current vision-language models. General-purpose and medical vision-language models and an open-vocabulary detector recalled 3% or fewer of cardiac structures and scored below a box that never sees the image. EchoLens, a detector trained on 5,912 expert-annotated structures and 4,219 Doppler signals from 136 patients, recalled 87% and localized structures as reliably as a blinded expert reader (box centre within the reference in 95.7% and 95.3% of cases). It covers 21 structures across 11 transthoracic views and 11 spectral Doppler signal types.…

items.title: Generative AI Versus Primary Care Physicians from Plan Initiation to Long-Term Maintenance of Chronic Disease Self-Management: A Vignette-Based Validation Study
items.summary: Background Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may provide personalised and dynamically adjustable support for chronic disease self-management. However, previous studies have largely focused on isolated questions and a limited range of evaluation dimensions. Objective To compare the quality of self-management advice generated by GenAI and primary care physicians (PCPs) across multiple stages of chronic disease management and evaluation dimensions. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional, source-blinded comparative evaluation using 15 standardised vignettes of diabetes and hypertension derived from authentic primary care follow-up records.…

items.title: AToP: An Explainability Framework for Transformer-Based EHR Predictions Using Attribution-Guided Temporal Pattern Mining
items.summary: Objective: To develop and evaluate AToP (Attribution to Temporal Patterns), a post-hoc explainability framework that converts per-token Integrated Gradients (IG) from a Transformer into structured temporal pattern narratives. Materials and Methods: AToP was applied to a single-stream Transformer trained on MIMIC-IV v3.1 (218,196 patients; 12.6% unplanned 30-day readmission). It mines frequent episodes from salient-token subsequences in the training cohort, aggregates attribution among patients whose records contain each token or pattern, and collapses near-duplicates by patient overlap. Validation used masking, reversed-order analysis, token-level faithfulness tests, and KernelSHAP comparison. Results: The Transformer achieved AUROC 0.77 and PR-AUC 0.34. Population-weighted attribution emphasized high-prevalence codes with small per-patient impact.…

items.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
items.summary: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice. We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on visual question answering and language benchmarks at matched lifetime compute.…
items.tldr: Controlled experiments show that multimodal language models do not need a pretrained vision encoder, but benefit from dedicated vision capacity trained jointly with the backbone and integrated early rather than before fusion.

items.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
items.summary: Second-order optimizers (e.g., Shampoo, SOAP) have emerged as compelling alternatives to Adam/AdamW and promise faster per-step convergence than AdamW in transformer training. However, they still remain costly in practice, and even SOAP still pays substantial optimizer-state memory and eigendecomposition overhead. We ask whether the benefits of SOAP can be retained at nearly the efficiency of AdamW. In this paper, we answer yes with a lightweight SOAP variant, Factored One-sided Adam-Moment (FOAM). The path to practical impact is twofold: first, FOAM employs input-only preconditioning, dropping the output-side Kronecker factor to reduce memory and remove one eigendecomposition. The Kronecker structure of the Hessian shows that this is exact for a diagonal output-side curvature and nearly lossless for a near-diagonal one, as we observe empirically.…
items.tldr: FOAM is a lightweight SOAP variant that uses input-only preconditioning and a factored Adam-moment estimator to match strong second-order and Muon baselines in LLM pre-training while using half the optimizer state and running at Muon-class speed.

items.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
items.summary: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. Large language models (LLMs) possess physical knowledge, but struggle to reliably guide video generation models in producing their training videos. We present PhysLoop, a unified harness designed to support physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models. The harness guides and constrains LLMs throughout video generation, selection, and correction, distilling their physical knowledge into physically consistent videos. The framework supports controllable training-data construction and inference-time video repair.…
items.tldr: PhysLoop leverages large language models to guide video generation, selection, and correction, enabling physically consistent self-improvement and controllable data construction for video models.

items.title: EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming
items.summary: Generalist manipulation policies can benefit from the complementary experience of humans, real robots, and simulated agents. However, differences in morphology, sensing, and control interfaces make it difficult to learn effectively from their combined demonstrations. We introduce EgoX, an egocentric cross-embodiment learning framework that organizes heterogeneous demonstrations through semantically corresponding observation and action modalities. EgoX pretrains a Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming (MXT+) on this mixture and fine-tunes it on target-embodiment demonstrations. Within each embodiment, MXT+ assigns a dedicated tokenizer to each observation modality and a dedicated expert to each action modality, with a Transformer trunk shared across embodiments.…
tags: Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming (MXT+)
items.tldr: EgoX is an egocentric cross-embodiment learning framework that pretrains a modular Transformer with embodiment dreaming on heterogeneous human, robot, and simulated demonstrations, then fine-tunes it to improve manipulation task progress, especially under out-of-distribution conditions.

items.title: Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: It is common to train Large Language Models (LLMs) for agentic tasks with Reinforcement Learning (RL) from scalar rewards. However, this throws away the fine-grained information about the environment that the agent experienced during the trial (e.g., error logs). To utilize this rich information, recent works wrap the agent in a harness that refines its own inputs through reflection or compaction and hands past experience to future rollouts, but the construction of the handed-off artifacts (e.g., a playbook) is itself not learned. We want the best of both worlds: gradient updates from a scalar reward, while also utilizing environment information to hand off experience. As a concrete testbed, we fix the Agentic Context Engineering (\ace{}) harness and train one model to act, reflect, and curate task-local playbooks.…
items.tldr: Language-model agents trained with reinforcement learning can improve by learning to create and curate experience artifacts that help future rollouts, not just by optimizing actions from scalar rewards.

items.title: UniSpark: Exploring Hybrid Attention for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
items.summary: We present UniSpark-9B, a unified multimodal model that investigates hybrid attention for visual understanding and generation. Built on a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts backbone with approximately 9B parameters in each branch, UniSpark combines full attention for explicit token interactions with GatedDeltaNet linear attention for compact context propagation. Autoregressive text prediction and visual flow matching jointly support visual question answering, text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and interleaved text-image prediction. In interleaved generation, noisy visual targets are isolated from subsequent predictions, while clean visual representations provide context for later outputs. A blockwise protocol enforces this distinction through attention masks in full-attention layers and recurrent-state retention rules in linear-attention layers.…

items.title: WorldDraft: If Code Builds the World, Can Video Models Just Render It?
items.summary: Multimodal coding agents decouple 4D world construction from visual generation, repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers. This division of labor raises a fundamental question: if code builds the world, can video models just render it? A reliable generative renderer hinges on two complementary criteria: (i) world preservation, retaining prescribed 4D kinematics and camera paths; and (ii) visual realization, persistently binding text-specified target attributes over time. To evaluate this capability, we introduce WorldDraft, a benchmark of $432$ strictly paired test cases across $48$ executable 4D world families spanning six dynamic challenge categories. Under a $3 \times 3$ factorial design, WorldDraft orthogonally crosses draft granularity (abstract proxy to previs) and appearance alignment (neutral to conflicting) under identical dynamics.…

items.title: From Large Language Models to Efficient System One Models via Adaptive Computation
items.summary: Transferring LLMs into System One decision models typically replaces the language modeling head with a decision head while retaining the full backbone, making every decision pay for all layers. Yet it remains unclear how much depth such decisions require. We find that decision information is concentrated in intermediate layers, with early layers building essential features and the final six layers removable without loss, while independently trained smaller models largely mimic the full model rather than developing specialized decision capabilities. These findings suggest that efficiency requires not simply smaller backbones, but shared computation across different depths. Building on this, we propose \method{}, which jointly trains a full model with prefix sub-models that share its final layers and decision head through self-distillation.…

items.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well. We compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld, and use JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop. As actors, all six models are pulled away from a subgoal that must come first by an easier one. As judges that see the whole trajectory, the same models credit the steps toward that subgoal, and asking whether each action helped, rather than whether the task will succeed, separates useful from useless actions.…
items.tldr: A decision model that acts poorly can still teach reinforcement learning policies effectively by judging complete action trajectories, improving success on ALFWorld and WebShop.

items.title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
items.summary: Large foundation models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 have recently been shown to control robots directly from visual observations. They nevertheless remain brittle on long-horizon, contact-rich tasks in real-world environments. Further progress depends on two complementary resources: demonstrations of human behavior that supervise how tasks are performed, and interactive environments in which policies can be rolled out, evaluated, and improved in closed loop. Language models have advanced along well-characterized scaling laws; the corresponding question for physical AI is how capability scales with environments and behaviors, which first requires identifying which data to scale and how to produce and reuse such data continuously.…

items.title: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
items.summary: Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models (LVSMs) with KV-cache have recently achieved state-of-the-art quality by regressing novel views from neural networks without reconstructing 3D geometry, while Test-Time Training (TTT) layers save computation but sacrifice quality. We propose Test-Time Baking (TTB), a strategy that learns to bake global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, enabling fast and high-fidelity novel-view decoding. The first key is to repurpose the fast-weight MLP of TTT to learn the cross-view attention mapping explicitly from its input-output pairs, rather than replacing attention entirely, achieving the same rendering efficiency as TTT while delivering substantially higher quality.…
items.tldr: By baking global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, Test-Time Baking (TTB) enhances the fidelity of novel-view decoding in Large View Synthesis Models while maintaining the efficiency of Test-Time Training.

items.title: Consensus Capture in Reference-Based UAV Video Stabilization: A Benchmark on Dynamic Urban Scenes
items.summary: Reference-frame stabilization registers every frame of a hovering-drone video onto one reference frame, keeping object positions comparable. The registration pipelines it relies on are selected on feature-matching benchmarks in which only the camera moves. Over a busy intersection, vehicles moving together supply mutually consistent correspondences that can draw the robust homography estimate toward their motion: consensus capture, which inlier statistics cannot flag. A two-part benchmark measures it and the object masking meant to prevent it. A static protocol scores ten pipelines under exactly known homographies on 4K aerial frames, tuned on a site-disjoint split at a matched resolution and feature budget.…

items.title: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents
items.summary: While search agents demonstrate impressive capabilities in multi-step question answering, their robustness to poor-quality evidence remains under-explored. Such evidence is rare in benchmark corpora, and resulting failures are hard to reproduce. We propose DeepStress, a dynamic stress-testing framework that subjects agents to degraded evidence at controlled rates. It replaces the retrieval module with a synthetic environment where documents are generated dynamically for each query, under independent control of their trustworthiness, relevance, and factuality. To characterize behavior under stress, we go beyond binary accuracy with a five-way classification of final-answer outcomes and two new reliability-aware metrics, RAS and CoPRAS, which credit cautious behavior and account for computational cost.…
items.tldr: A dynamic stress-testing framework shows that search agents often answer confidently despite unreliable retrieved evidence and may rely on memorized knowledge when documents are factually wrong.

items.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
items.summary: Frontier video generation models work in a VAE latent space that compresses video in both space and time. This compression made training tractable, but now limits high-resolution, controllable, and interactive generation -- doubling resolution quadruples token count, conditions apply to groups of frames rather than individual ones, and each response must wait for the rest of its multi-frame block. We present PixVid, a simple yet effective method that lifts a pretrained latent video model to directly generate every frame in pixel space. PixVid keeps the diffusion transformer and replaces the VAE decoder with a convolutional head that renders its outputs into pixels. We find that predicting clean video rather than velocity, together with a larger noise shift, is key to quality. Finetuned from Wan2.1-14B, PixVid is competitive with the latent baseline within sim 1.3M training clips.…

items.title: The Value of Thinking: Learning When to Reason in Hybrid Decision Models
items.summary: Existing adaptive-reasoning methods shorten the explicit reasoning a model writes, or skip it by switching modes; either way the answer is still written out token by token. Rather than deciding how much to think, we explore a different paradigm, zero-or-T thinking: a single model either answers from the implicit thinking inside one forward pass, generating no token, or performs full autoregressive reasoning at a cost of T tokens when that is worth paying. We realise it in a hybrid decision model (HDM), where one frozen backbone serves both modes and a lightweight self-routing block chooses between them. The block estimates the value of thinking, the utility the slow mode is expected to add over the fast one, from what that implicit thinking has already produced, and the slow mode runs only where that value exceeds a price λ set per request.…
items.tldr: A hybrid decision model routes between implicit single-forward-pass answering and full autoregressive reasoning via a self-routing block trained with calibrated decision policy optimization, reducing token and latency costs while preserving accuracy.

items.title: Hypothesis-Driven Identification of Neural Algorithms With Dynamical Structure-Preserving Manifolds.
items.summary: Neuroscience aims to uncover the algorithms by which the brain builds and manipulates rich internal representations of objects, agents, and places. Existing reverse-engineering frameworks remain ineffective for identifying these algorithms. Here, we present Dynamical Structure-Preserving Manifolds (dSPMs)---a novel multilevel reverse-engineering framework that programs, without training, recurrent neural networks to enable hypothesis-driven identification of the brain's algorithms that generate symbolic, structure-preserving representations of the world around. We apply dSPM to identify an algorithm for physical scene prediction in the dorsomedial frontal cortex (DMFC) of macaques intercepting a ball on a Pong-like virtual gameboard.…

items.title: Polysemanticity in human hippocampal neurons
items.summary: As we perceive language, neurons in the brain represent the meanings of each word we hear. Inspired by recent advances in the mechanistic interpretability of large language models (LLMs), we hypothesized that hippocampal neurons utilize polysemanticity, a coding strategy wherein individual neurons represent multiple semantically distant features. Polysemanticity increases capacity, robustness, and scalability, and facilitates contextualization. We find that during podcast listening, hippocampal single neurons exhibit dense semantic codes characterized by multiple tuning peaks. These peaks, corresponding to the stimuli that most effectively drive the neurons, are not random; instead, they have overdispersed, isotropic geometry, consistent with interference-minimizing repulsive coding, although they lack grid-like hexagonal structure.…

items.title: Learning Interpretable Switching Dynamics in Shared Neural-Behavioral Latent Space
items.summary: Modern recording technologies enable simultaneous measurement of high-dimensional neural activity and rich behavioral variables, creating both an opportunity and a modeling challenge: identifying the shared latent structure that mediates the brain-behavior relationship and the underlying dynamics through which it evolves across behavioral states. Existing approaches focus on different parts of this challenge: shared representation learning methods identify neural-behavioral subspaces but typically do not model dynamical structure, while dynamical models capture temporal variation and discrete state transitions in neural activity, but do not explicitly disentangle shared neural-behavioral structure from modality-specific variability.…

items.title: Pallatom2: Navigating the De Novo Protein Universe with Atom-to-Atom Modeling
items.summary: Protein binder design requires precise coordination of molecular structure, binding geometry, and experimentally measurable performance. We introduce Pallatom2, an efficient, precise Atom-to-Atom generative model that jointly models protein sequence, backbone conformation, side-chain geometry, and target-interface contacts. A unified Atom14 representation and residue-guided sparse all-atom attention enable bidirectional information exchange between residue-level and atom-level representations, coordinating global structure with local atomic detail in a compact model of just 65.9 million parameters. Its conditioning system provides fine-grained control over binder-target engagement and global and local protein conformations, supporting diverse target-specific design requirements.…

items.title: ProLigGPT: a language model for protein-targeted ligand design free from structural constraints
items.summary: The deep-learning language model offers promising approaches to molecular design. However, existing models typically exhibit one or more of the following limitations: structural constraints, confinement to a single task, and lack of cross-domain capability (e.g., protein-to-ligand generation). Inspired by GPT's success in language modeling, we introduce ProLigGPT, a seq2seq autoregressive model based on GPT-2 and trained on ~1.9 million protein-ligand pairs without 3D structures. ProLigGPT supports tasks including de novo ligand generation and scaffold-based molecular design for target proteins. Benchmarking against three state-of-the-art structure-based models across eight representative target proteins, ProLigGPT demonstrated superior performance on comprehensive metrics.…

items.title: Image-Conditioned Diffusion Preserves Latent PhysiologicalSignals and Enables Cross-Site Transfer of Synthetic MedicalImages
items.summary: Medical imaging models depend on large, shareable datasets, yet privacy constraints limit data dissemination. Text-conditioned diffusion models generate only what the prompt specifies and can miss subtle, distributed clinical signals, such as continuous physiological biomarkers, that downstream physiological models rely on. Here we systematically evaluate image-conditioned (I2I) diffusion, which anchors generation to a real source image. Fine-tuning Stable Diffusion on retinal fundus photographs from the Human Phenotype Project, we find that I2I-synthetic images retain more source-specific signal than text-conditioned generation, including for biomarkers absent from the prompt (hemoglobin, waist circumference).…

items.title: Volumetric Analysis of the Deltoid Muscle From Neck-to-Knee Dixon MRI: A pilot population assessment of a posterior intramuscular injection target
items.summary: Abstract Background: Deltoid muscle volume varies across anatomical regions and population groups, with potential implications for intramuscular injection site selection. Evidence comparing middle and posterior deltoid volumes in vaccine-eligible populations is limited. Purpose: To compare middle and posterior deltoid muscle volumes by vaccine eligibility group, sex, and side. Methods: Deltoid muscles were manually segmented into anterior, middle and posterior regions in 43 UK Biobank Dixon MRI scans. A MONAI deep learning model trained on the annotations (Dice score = 0.78) segmented deltoid muscles of 5,239 participants, categorised by UK flu vaccination eligibility: A ([≥]65 years without risk conditions, n=1,760), B ([≥]65 years with risk conditions, n=1,744), and C (<65 with risk conditions, n=1,735).…

items.title: Detecting Contradictory Evidence on Drug-Disease Associations at Scale
items.summary: Contradictory claims about drug efficacy across randomized controlled trials (RCTs) complicate evidence-based medicine, yet existing automated methods classify isolated sentence pairs and do not explain why studies disagree. We present DrugCon, a large language model (LLM)-based framework that extracts study conclusions from RCT abstracts, links these claims when they concern the same drug-disease association, detects contradictions with counterfactual reasoning, and explains them using a taxonomy of ten study-level factors such as population, dosage, and outcome measures. Applying DrugCon to 224,756 RCT abstracts, we built DrugCon-Bench, an exhaustively annotated benchmark of 542 contradictory claim pairs from 819 abstracts. Most contradictions involve more than one study-level factor (75.5%).…

items.title: Assessment of Undergraduate Psychological Wellbeing Using Explainable Machine Learning: A Study from Sri Lanka
items.summary: Academic, psychosocial, financial, environmental, and interpersonal factors are widely recognized as important contributors to the overall wellbeing of students. This study aimed to identify factors associated with the psychological wellbeing of university undergraduates and compare the performance of machine learning models for binary and multiclass classification of wellbeing status using self-reported survey data from undergraduates at the University of Peradeniya, Sri Lanka. The findings may facilitate the early identification of students with lower wellbeing and inform targeted interventions to foster a healthier and more supportive academic environment. Cross-sectional questionnaire data from 2,913 undergraduates were analyzed to classify psychological wellbeing using overall happiness scores.…

items.title: MENTOR: An Evidence-Informed Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent System for Efficient Selection of Institution-Specific Negative Control Outcomes
items.summary: Objective Negative control outcomes (NCOs) help detect and correct systematic error in observational studies, yet their selection remains largely manual. The Common Evidence Model (CEM) can generate candidate lists, but researchers must still screen them for plausibility as true nulls and for sufficient observation in each institution's data. We developed and evaluated MENTOR (Multi-agent Evidence-informed Negative conTrol Outcome selection with Reasoning), a multi-agent system of large language models (LLMs) that combines CEM evidence with LLM reasoning to select institution-specific NCOs. Methods Four LLM agents operate on an institution's Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership common data model.…

items.title: DEVELOPMENT AND INTERNAL EVALUATION OF MODELS FOR PREDICTING PROLONGED HOSPITALISATION AMONG PATIENTS WITH SICKLE CELL DISEASE IN A PUBLIC UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL IN GHANA
items.summary: Background: Prolonged hospitalisation is an important burden among patients with sickle cell disease (SCD), with implications for healthcare utilisation and patient and caregiver burden. Early prediction may support timely clinical and resource-management interventions. Objective: To identify factors associated with prolonged hospitalisation among patients with SCD and compare the predictive performance of multivariable logistic regression with five supervised machine-learning algorithms. Methods: This retrospective study included SCD inpatients aged [≥]16 years admitted to the University of Ghana Hospital between January 2019 and December 2024. Logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, support vector machine, and k-nearest neighbours models were developed using five-fold stratified cross-validation. Class weighting and SMOTE were applied within training folds.…

items.title: Geospatial AI targeting of tuberculosis active case finding in Pune, India: a quasi-experimental evaluation
items.summary: BACKGROUND: Active case finding (ACF) in India screens large populations to find few cases. AI-NETRA predicts neighbourhood-level tuberculosis (TB) risk from routine notification data and generates field microplans. OBJECTIVE: To compare the yield and efficiency of AI-guided and standard ACF, and frontline acceptability. DESIGN: Prospective quasi-experimental evaluation in four TB Units of Pune district, comparing two-week AI-guided sweeps (April to May 2026) with the routine campaign in the same units (December 2024 to January 2025). Primary endpoint: bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB per persons screened; secondary: all-forms yield, presumptive yield, referral precision, number needed to screen (NNS) and cost per case. Acceptability: 16 focus groups (n=100) and a survey of 101 ASHAs.…

items.title: Trait-Level Rather Than Individual-Level Resolution in Fitness Genomics: A Population-Calibrated Variant Prioritization Framework in a South Asian Cohort
items.summary: Translating candidate gene panels into objective physiological trait interpretations remains a major hurdle in exercise genomics. Conventional total genotype scoring suffers from severe panel-composition bias, fails to evaluate unannotated or novel variants, and frequently fosters inflated claims regarding individual athletic prediction. Here, we present a population-calibrated, multi-tiered computational framework that evaluates genomic variation across six evidence streams integrating deep learning protein and genomic language models (ESM-2, Evo 2), missense and splice predictors (AlphaMissense, SpliceAI), and regional pathogenic-density metrics to generate a continuous Variant Priority Score (VPS; 1-10 scale). By dynamically renormalizing missing evidence streams rather than zero-filling them, the framework robustly scores unannotated variants lacking empirical database entries.…

items.title: Quantum Control
items.summary: Quantum Control is the art of steering the fragile dynamics of a quantum system in a precise way toward a desired final state or transformation. It is a cornerstone of many quantum technology applications and at the same time allows us to shed light on the fundamental connection between the energy structure and the time dynamics of quantum systems at the heart of some of the most interesting phenomena of quantum mechanics. In this chapter on quantum control, we introduce the control problem, go through basic error sources and methods to suppress these errors and then discuss state-of-the-art techniques to solve the control problem, like adiabatic methods, quantum optimal control and methods of machine learning.

items.title: Robo-SWE: An Executable Issue-Resolution Dataset Mined from Robot Software Repositories
items.summary: Coding agents are evaluated mostly on general-purpose software, but domain-specific systems require domain-aware evaluation. Robot software is a particularly challenging case: Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) packages have their own build tools, simulators and learning frameworks are built on physics engines, and behavior that depends on timing and hardware is hard to test. We present Robo-SWE, a dataset of 236 executable issue-resolution tasks mined from merged pull requests in 28 public robotics repositories in four domains: ROS 2 systems, simulation and physics engines, robotics algorithm libraries, and robot-learning frameworks. Each task contains the original issue text, a container recipe for the repository at the commit before the fix, the developers' fix, and the developers' tests, which fail before the fix and pass after it in repeated offline runs.…

items.title: Trained on What Screen Readers Cannot Read: Accessibility Debt in the GUI Corpora Behind Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Computer-use agents learn to operate mobile interfaces from corpora of captured screens and accessibility trees. The same trees are what a screen reader consumes, so an agent trained on them inherits whatever labelling gaps the underlying applications carry. This paper measures one of those gaps, content-description coverage, in two Android corpora: Rico, collected in 2017, and AndroidControl, collected in 2024. Across 17,373,614 interface elements, 17.74% of the Rico elements that need a content description under our coding rule carry one, against 57.27% in AndroidControl. The difference of 39.5 percentage points holds under five alternative coding rules and when whole apps are resampled. It describes two datasets that also differ in app selection, capture method and platform version; it does not measure change over time.…

items.title: Show Your Work in Swahili: Reinforcement Learning for Native-Language Mathematical Reasoning
items.summary: We present Fikiria, a two-stage SFT+GRPO recipe for Swahili mathematical reasoning. Its reward multiplies a format gate by a weighted sum of answer accuracy and the ChrF\texttt{++} similarity of the Swahili reasoning to an in-language reference chain of thought, so that training targets the surface fidelity of the reasoning trace and not only the final answer. We train on a 2.3k-problem Swahili dataset created by translating GSM8K with GPT-4.1 and filtering with SSA-COMET. On AfriMGSM Swahili, Fikiria-AfriqueQwen-14B reaches 79.2\%. Under the same fixed prompt and strict answer-format scoring, GPT-4o reaches 68.0\%, partly because it often fails the required answer format; IrokoBench reports 78.8\% for GPT-4o using a best-per-model prompt, a figure numerically close to ours but not directly comparable.…

items.title: Subsurface schematisation from sparse CPT data using the tabular foundation model TabPFN
items.summary: Subsurface schematisation supports geotechnical decisions but remains challenging because sparse site-investigation data leave substantial gaps in information about ground conditions. This study explores TabPFN, a foundation model pretrained on general synthetic tabular data, for this task. Using only grid coordinates and soil behaviour type index observations from sparse cone penetration tests (CPTs), we first reconstruct two-dimensional sections without geotechnical fine-tuning or predefined layer boundaries. We evaluate the approach on synthetic sections and at two field sites in the Netherlands, comparing it with SchemaGAN, a conditional generative adversarial network trained on synthetic geotechnical sections, and with reference interpolation methods.…

items.title: Gradient-Aware AI Agents for Autonomous Turbulence Model Discovery via Differentiable CFD
items.summary: Turbulence modeling relies on human choices of closure form, physical inputs, and tunable parameters. Training closures a posteriori is efficient only with gradients through long chaotic rollouts, which few solvers provide. Most a posteriori approaches therefore resort to gradient-free optimization, and nearly all fix the closure form in advance, learning only its parameters. In this work, we introduce a gradient-aware agentic framework that poses closure discovery as a bilevel problem: a multi-agent large language model (LLM) system searches over closure forms, while a GPU-native differentiable computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solver supplies gradients, making differentiable a posteriori learning an action of the autonomous AI agent.…

items.title: TGen-SQD: Physics-Informed Transferable Configuration Generator for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization
items.summary: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) avoids iterative variational circuit optimization, but its accuracy and cost depend on selecting a compact determinant subspace that captures the ground state. Existing machine-learning selectors use task-specific physical cues and typically retrain for each Hamiltonian. We introduce TGen-SQD, a physics-informed generator jointly trained across multiple Hamiltonians. It learns from configuration-interaction-weighted data and uses orbital- and system-level descriptors to guide generation. After training, its weights remain frozen for inference on seen and zero-shot geometries. On a 20-qubit H10 chain, TGen-SQD achieves mean energy errors of 40.18 +/- 1.52 and 43.97 +/- 1.20 mHa on seen and unseen geometries, respectively, 12.7% and 11.7% lower than the state-of-the-art PIGen-SQD baseline under matched shot and proposal budgets.

items.title: Vocabulary-Free Next-Event Prediction on Temporal Graphs
items.summary: Autoregressive transformer training through next-token prediction has driven remarkable advances in language modeling and has become increasingly effective for time-series modeling. Yet its success in temporal graph learning remains limited, and most temporal link-prediction methods are discriminative rather than autoregressive. While temporal graphs can have a natural serialization through chronological ordering edges, they lack an obvious graph-independent tokenization: existing node tokenization often uses a vocabulary that grows with the number of nodes, limiting scalability and cross-graph training. We propose GTGT, Generative Temporal Graph Transformer, a simple yet powerful vocabulary-free framework for self-supervised next-event prediction on temporal graphs.…

items.title: Pothole Risk Assessment with Geometrically Grounded Vision Language Models
items.summary: Potholes impose billions of dollars in annual vehicle damage, yet detectors report only where potholes are, not how severe they are or what to do. Judging severity from a single RGB image is ill-posed, and ungrounded vision-language model (VLM) assessments tend to be over-conservative. We present a five-stage modular framework for the offline assessment of already-detected potholes that combines geometric measurements with VLM reasoning: perspective transformation, zero-shot SAM segmentation, geometric feature extraction, Gemini 2.5 Pro severity classification with composite risk scoring, and natural-language warning generation. We evaluate it on 3,092 potholes in 1,119 dashcam scenes against independent references.…

items.title: Pyramidal Columns Acting as Attention Heads
items.summary: Can the functional architecture of a Transformer attention head be given a biological construction? More specifically, could a suitable group of pyramidal columns in posterior temporal language regions (PTLRs) constitute the biological construction of a neuromorphic mechanical realization of an attention head, under a mathematical instantiation that need not coincide with its standard Transformer instantiation? This paper investigates this hypothesis by examining possible correspondences between the functional organization of attention heads and neurophysiological mechanisms operating within and across pyramidal columns involved in human language processing. Our analysis builds on a mechanical-structural description of Transformer attention heads as systems of simple neural networks linked through output-input and output-weight interconnections.…

items.title: Your PID Is Already a Neural Network: Learning Its Gains with Only Three Weights and No Teacher
items.summary: A discrete PID controller is exactly a recurrent neural network, a classical state-space fact: a fixed linear memory of the running integral and the last error, read out by three trainable weights that map one-to-one to the PID gains. Networks with bounded hidden states, such as LSTMs of any width, only approximate it. Trained only on a one-step physical cost (the expected cost of one transition from a fixed state distribution), with no demonstrations, teacher controller, or known gains, the network solves a strongly convex least-squares problem, so gradient descent converges from any initialization to the unique one-step optimal PID gains; the limit network is that PID, with the same action on every error sequence. Partitioned regression then shows what extra capacity buys.…
