items.title: Routes of Reasoning: Reading and Reshaping Test-Time Compute in MoE Models
items.summary: Reasoning models allocate test-time compute across distinct behaviors such as planning, deriving, and verifying. However, models frequently "overthink," continuing to verify and re-derive long after finding a correct answer. This wastes expensive compute and can even degrade performance. Existing interventions, such as token budgets or steering, primarily regulate reasoning duration rather than targeting specific behaviors. In this work, we demonstrate that Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routers provide a natural, training-free interface for behavioral control. We first split reasoning traces into sentence-level segments and label each with one of six reasoning behaviors (planning, execution, restatement, fact, reflection, and conclusion), so that every token carries the behavior of its segment.…

items.title: Autonomous agents for electricity-system planning
items.summary: Planning electricity systems requires repeated decisions that connect regional resources, investment, operation and network constraints. Here we present an autonomous planning framework that carries prepared regional scenarios through proposal, numerical evaluation, feedback interpretation, redesign and final plan selection. Agents propose investment bounds, storage operating conditions and feeder interventions, interpret numerical feedback, and decide how to revise designs and when to stop. The framework automatically executes annual investment-and-dispatch optimization and representative-feeder verification, applies fixed acceptance criteria and retains the lowest-cost accepted candidate.…

items.title: Does Your Trial Simulator Know What the Drug Does? An Intervention-Blind Test of Interventional Validity on 7,207 Registered Trials
items.summary: Patient world models are increasingly proposed as simulators of clinical trials, and recent surveys rank their capabilities on a ladder from temporal prediction to counterfactual rollouts. Position on that ladder is currently assigned by reading papers rather than by measurement. We turn the counterfactual rung into a measured quantity. From 30,119 completed phase 2/3 trials with results posted to ClinicalTrials.gov we construct 9,996 audited within-trial contrasts from 7,207 trials, and we score a simulator on how much of its accuracy depends on knowing which intervention was tested. The instrument is an intervention-blind reference: the same model, trained on the same trials, with every intervention-identifying field withheld. Interventional skill is the error the full model removes relative to that reference.…

items.title: CHARM+: Cross-Hardware Attention with Re-Merge Multistream Mechanism
items.summary: As sequence lengths continue to grow, distributed attention based on sequence parallel (e.g., Ring-Attention) has become a mainstream solution for large language models (LLMs). Nevertheless, inherent communication dependencies limit computation-communication overlap, reducing GPU utilization. Moreover, in cross-hardware (NUMA or node) architectures, due to imbalanced communication bandwidth, frequent communication synchronization will limit overall performance. Based on these insights, we propose CHARM+, Cross-Hardware Attention with Re-Merge Multistream Mechanism. We reorganize sequential communications into several levels and achieve intra-level parallelism and computation overlap. Furthermore, we decouple cross-hardware communication from intra-hardware communication, eliminating synchronization overhead caused by bandwidth imbalance.…

items.title: Retrieval Supersedes Scale: Efficient Log Level Prediction via Multiplex Socio-Technical Context
items.summary: Developers insert logging statements in source code to record its execution, and the resulting logs are essential for detecting and troubleshooting system anomalies. A key part of these statements is the log level (e.g., DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR), which determines whether a message is recorded. Choosing it is a trade-off: levels set too low mask important information in production, while levels set too high create noisy logs and extra I/O and storage overhead. Recent work uses Large Language Models (LLMs) with In-Context Learning (ICL) to predict log levels, but typically augments the prompt with randomly sampled examples. We argue that this overlooks the socio-technical nature of logging, where conventions vary by component and development team.…

items.title: Weaver: Weaving Preference Evidence through Incremental Reasoning for Personalized Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: Personalized retrieval-augmented generation requires extracting and applying user preferences from extended interaction histories. This task is challenging because preference evidence is scattered across past conversations and remains bound to specific temporal and situational contexts. Consequently, isolated fragments rarely provide complete support for a response, while preferences expressed under different conditions are easily conflated. To address these limitations, we propose Weaver, a framework that incrementally weaves memory-conditioned retrieval trajectories with compositional preference reasoning for personalized responses. Weaver operates on a Dual-Layer Retrieval and Reasoning Graph that couples an upper Intent Dependency Graph with a lower Memory-Conditioned Retrieval Trajectory Graph.…

items.title: FWIK: Multi-Waypoint IK Selection via Lookahead Graph Search
items.summary: An ordered sequence of end-effector poses can give a redundant robot arm multiple valid joint configurations at each waypoint. Inverse kinematics (IK) computes these configurations. Choosing a configuration only for the next waypoint can leave the arm poorly placed for later waypoints. This may increase planned motion time or cause a later planning failure. This paper presents Future-Window Inverse Kinematics (FWIK), an online method that selects IK solutions by considering a small window of future waypoints. FWIK generates several IK candidates, connects them in a layered joint-space graph, and ranks candidate paths with a simple motion-time estimate. A learned model removes paths whose transitions are likely to cause self-collision.…

items.title: Transformer-Based Characterization of Criticality in Directed Percolation
items.summary: Directed percolation (DP) provides a canonical framework for studying nonequilibrium phase transitions into absorbing states, yet extracting critical behavior directly from high-dimensional spatiotemporal configurations remains challenging. Here, we investigate (1 + 1)- and (2 + 1)-dimensional bond DP using a supervised Transformer encoder. Supervised learning results demonstrate that the Transformer can distinguish between the active and absorbing phases of directed percolation with high accuracy. The critical point and critical exponents estimated from the model's classification probabilities align closely with reference values from existing literature, indicating that the model not only achieves phase classification but also yields outputs containing information related to critical scaling behavior.…

items.title: CellCanon: An Agentic Cellular World Model for Prediction, Explanation, and Observation-Driven Updating
items.summary: Biological discovery requires using molecular knowledge and new measurements to infer responses beyond the conditions already observed. We introduce CellCanon, the first agentic cellular world model to unify single-cell expression prediction, evidence-grounded explanation, and observation-driven updating. Its predictive core reuses condition-level biological evidence across gene-specific numerical readouts to guide single-cell expression generation. A shared world state links predictions, acquired measurements, and source-linked claims, supporting explanation and revision. On 339 held-out SciPlex3 conditions across three cell lines, CellCanon improves differential-expression AUPRC and Macro-F1 over the best baseline for each metric by 63.3% and 17.3%, respectively, and direction Macro-F1 by 7.2%.…

items.title: Hardware Demonstration of Neural-Surrogated Quantum-Enhanced MCMC for Large-Scale Constrained Boltzmann Sampling
items.summary: Neural-surrogated quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QeMCMC) uses neural networks trained on samples from the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) to accelerate Boltzmann sampling. A divide-and-conquer strategy extends this approach to larger systems, but independently optimizing QAOA parameters for each subproblem is costly. In this paper, we develop a hardware-efficient implementation of neural-surrogated QeMCMC and demonstrate it using an IBM Quantum Heron r2 processor. Experiments with $N=144$ binary variables reveal faster autocorrelation decay for appropriate subproblem sizes while exposing challenges in neural-surrogate learning for larger blocks. We then extend the demonstration to a system with $N=1064$, where the autocorrelation decay rate per MCMC step is approximately $5.2$ and $12.3$ times those of global and local Kawasaki dynamics, respectively.…

items.title: MIGONet: a multiple-input graph neural operator with solver-free discrete manufactured-solution training
items.summary: Surrogate modeling of transport requires operators that capture the combined influence of spatially distributed sources and Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, together with training datasets that can be generated at low computational cost. This work presents MIGONet, a multiple-input graph neural operator, and a discrete method of manufactured solutions (MMS) that trains it without solving a partial differential equation, using steady heat conduction as the model problem. In the discrete MMS procedure, temperature fields are prescribed a priori, and the source terms and Dirichlet or Neumann boundary data are evaluated with the same discrete operators as the reference finite-difference method (FDM), so every training sample satisfies the discrete governing equations by construction.…

items.title: Generative AI for urban planning: synthesizing land-use maps with satellite imagery via DualControlNet
items.summary: Various land-use models characterize land-use patterns and facilitate scenario planning. However, existing models are largely predictive, forecasting transitions based on numeric data without synthesizing new land-use maps from simple text prompts. Meanwhile, generative AI in urban systems remains unimodal, weakly controllable, and evaluated mostly by generic image quality rather than domain-specific metrics. To address these gaps, we introduce DualControlNet, a generative land-use model that jointly synthesizes high-resolution land-use maps and satellite imagery, addressing multimodality, controllability, and verification challenges. Trained on over 40,000 paired tiles from Orlando and Chicago, DualControlNet is evaluated using land-use, spatial consistency, and image quality metrics.…

items.title: Risk Control Certifies Rates, Not Magnitudes: An Audit of Selective Fetal Biometry
items.summary: Prenatal ultrasound biometry must return a head circumference (HC) and refuse when the image cannot support one. Selective prediction trades coverage against error, but its finite-sample guarantees bound the rate of gross errors, not their magnitude. We audit a tool-grounded biometry pipeline on two separately pre-registered four-way splits of the 999 labelled HC18 images, retraining the segmenter three times on each. Calibrating the contour-completeness threshold by exact Clopper-Pearson risk control returns a certificate indistinguishable from a hand-set floor, yet the pipeline still emits a 271.3 mm error: a small, geometrically complete ring fitted to an image whose true HC is 324.6 mm. The accepted candidate scores 0.94 completeness, so the score cannot see the failure, and one outlier among $\approx 150$ answers leaves the certified risk bound ($α= 0.10$) intact.…

items.title: ricursiveAI/Ripple-65B-Preview
A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction
items.summary: Foundation-model predictors of perturbation response are evaluated primarily by aggregate accuracy. Using their predictions to prioritize experiments requires assessing each prediction's reliability. We audit the state-transition (ST) decoder used in STATE across three encoders (SE-600M, scGPT, and Tahoe-x1) and four cell lines under CRISPRi. The decoder's first attention layer has a low-rank output. Projecting this output onto 4-32 fixed directions estimated from training activations preserves mean per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC). This low-rank attention bottleneck bounds the decoder's reliability by distance to training responses: PDC declines as the cosine distance from a perturbation's observed response to its nearest training response increases.…

items.title: Time-to-Goal: Learned Temporal Metrics for Long-Horizon Planning with JEPA World Models
items.summary: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) support planning by comparing predicted latent states with an encoded goal. For this comparison to guide temporal progress, states closer in time to the goal should receive lower costs. However, training representations for prediction and distribution regularization does not directly enforce this ordering. We examine this mismatch in flat LeWorldModel (LeWM) by analyzing how its Euclidean goal cost changes with temporal separation. Our analysis identifies conditions under which states at different long offsets receive similar average costs, weakening their temporal distinction. To learn the missing ordering explicitly, we introduce Time-to-Goal (T2G), a lightweight metric trained on latent triples from offline trajectories.…

items.title: Neural Networks with Exciton-Polariton Waveguides
items.summary: We propose and numerically study a scheme for neural networks using exciton-polariton waveguide meshes. These enable arbitrary programmable interlayer couplings suited to a restricted Boltzmann machine architecture where polariton phases act as stochastic network variables. We show that such a network can be trained using unsupervised Hebbian and anti-Hebbian updates. This allows the implementation of an associative memory, where the network recovers learned patterns from imperfect inputs.

items.title: Vision Paper: Why Distributed LLM Post-Training and Decentralized Alignment Are Now Essential
items.summary: This vision paper argues that distributed learning, including federated and decentralized, should become a first-class paradigm in LLM post-training, not merely a privacy add-on. Current methods like RLHF and DPO rest on an invisible assumption: preference data should be centralized. We contend this assumption is scientifically unjustified, practically unsustainable, and ethically problematic. As LLMs deploy into healthcare, law, finance, and multilingual communities, preference data originates from populations that cannot or will not centralize. We develop a three-pillar argument grounded in (1) privacy and data sovereignty, (2) pluralism and representational equity, and (3) robustness and scalability.…

items.title: RACE: Calibrated Cumulative Scoring for Rollout-Free Robot Policy Checkpoint Selection
items.summary: Assessing the deployment performance of learned robot policies during training is challenging, as directly measuring task success requires costly real-world trials for each candidate checkpoint. Averaged validation loss offers a rollout-free alternative, but its checkpoint rankings can be inconsistent with deployment performance. We analyze two limitations of this criterion: it penalizes action deviations without considering whether the policy can recover from them, and gives later reference predictions equal weight even when earlier deviations may lead execution away from the reference. We propose RACE, a novel rollout-free metric for ranking checkpoints using a fixed set of held-out successful trajectories. RACE calibrates action deviations against state-conditional thresholds derived from action differences at similar states in these trajectories.…

items.title: Pathwise-Budgeted LLM Routing: Online Allocation with K-Bit Tail-Cost Learning
items.summary: Firms using large language models under fixed budgets must decide which model to call and whether to retry a failed task. Because a call's charge is revealed only after completion, one long response can exhaust the remaining budget and leave later tasks unserved. Our objective is to maximize the number of tasks solved before service stops. We develop a contextual bandit policy, ADP-HT, which learns each model's task-specific success probability and constructs conservative cost estimates from coarsened response-length labels on a quantile grid with $2^K$ intervals. The policy weighs predicted success against these costs, adjusting the cost penalty to realized spending and the budget available per remaining task. Under calibration, local regularity, and grid-coverage conditions, we bound the excess allowance in the policy's conservative cost estimates.…

items.title: Autonomy and Coordination in Intelligent Manufacturing: A Recursive Autonomous Agent Framework
items.summary: Intelligent production requires systems to make decisions and organize work according to production goals and operating conditions. It also requires continuous adjustment through feedback. This paper analyzes intelligence in human production organizations from a complex adaptive systems (CAS) perspective. The analysis identifies two coupled mechanisms: individual autonomy and collective coordination. Individual autonomy enables actors to form local decisions using available information. Collective coordination aligns these decisions with shared goals and joint constraints. Learning and adaptation improve both mechanisms over time. A production-system model formalizes how local decision rules and coordination jointly form system decisions.…

items.title: TandemBench: Benchmarking Decision Models for Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.summary: Decision models choose among predefined options in tasks such as routing and action selection. In multi-agent collaboration, a decision determines how members divide work, exchange resources, and act in parallel. We introduce TandemBench, a benchmark of 1,200 questions in multi-agent cooking scenarios where coordination choices affect goal completion. Models receive complete global information and candidate team plans, with reference answers established through execution and exact search. Models select an optimal team plan and, in paired variants that retain or remove it, judge whether better arrangements exist beyond the supplied options. We evaluate 40 native decision models and compare them with 10 general-purpose language models. The best native decision model achieves 62.50% decision accuracy. Native decision models remain close to chance in optimality verification.…

items.title: tencent/TailorRig
items.summary: TailorRig Human character rigging dataset: 39,073 humanoid meshes with skeletons and skinning weights, stored as .npz files and packed into four source-based subset archives. Suitable for training and evaluation of skeleton generation (auto-rigging), skinning-weight prediction (auto-skinning), joint-position regression, and related tasks.…

items.title: A Hybrid Approach for Automated Security Pattern Recovery
items.summary: Security-by-design emphasises integrating security into software design and development. Security pattern catalogues operationalise this principle by prescribing reusable architectural solutions to recurring security problems. However, recovering their implementations from source code remains challenging because security patterns are abstract, span multiple components, and admit many valid implementations. We present SecPatRec, a hybrid approach for automated security pattern recovery from source code repositories. We treat a security pattern as a reference architecture and frame its recovery as a deductive task: determining which prescribed roles are present, grounding them in code entities, and recovering their interaction sequences.…

items.title: Learning When Human Decisions Matter: Executor-Relative Consultation Value for LLM Agents
items.summary: Large language models increasingly automate complex tasks, but human decision capacity does not scale with their capabilities. In many applications, humans remain essential for providing private context, authority, or judgments unavailable to the agent. We formulate human decision capacity allocation: given multiple consultation opportunities and a limited budget, at which decisions should an LLM agent consult a human? The central challenge is estimating consultation value, which is executor-dependent because the same human input may benefit different downstream agents differently. We introduce Consultation Value Distillation (CVD), which estimates consultation values offline using Monte Carlo executor rollouts and distills these values into lightweight predictors for budgeted allocation, requiring no rollout-based value estimation at deployment.…

items.title: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Divergences in Office Documents
items.summary: Office documents are now routinely uploaded to large language models (LLMs) for processing. However, an LLM does not always see what a human sees, because it typically reads the text that an extractor produces from the document's underlying Office Open XML (OOXML) files. Depending on the implementation, extractors differ in which OOXML parts they read and how they interpret them, so their output can differ from what Office applications display. For example, by slightly shifting the positions of text boxes on a slide, an adversary can swap the order in which the model reads them while the slide looks unchanged. We show that this extraction divergence is an attack surface for LLM applications. In this work, we first measure what an adversary can exploit by analyzing the widely used extractors that LLM applications rely on.…

items.title: Item Representations Matter: Bridging Hard Semantic IDs and Soft Prototype Mixtures for Generative Retrieval
items.summary: Modern recommender systems rely on generative retrieval techniques to predict the next item either as discrete codes or as a continuous vector. On the one hand, Semantic IDs (SIDs) give discrete models shared parameters and pretrained semantic structure, but discretizing items into hard codes discards some information from the original content embeddings. On the other hand, continuous models avoid quantization, yet typically use flat item lookup tables with no explicit parameter tying across items. We ask whether a continuous recommender can introduce shared structure without making it a discrete bottleneck. We propose CAP-Mix, a flow recommender that represents each item as a soft mixture of shared prototypes plus an item-specific vector. The assignments, prototypes, and item vectors are trained jointly, and the soft representation is retained at inference.…

items.title: DARE: Difficulty Analysis for Repair Enhancement
items.summary: LLM-based coding agents are primarily evaluated by their solve rates. However, this metric does not reveal how difficult the solved tasks are or account for differences in task difficulty across benchmarks. Determining the difficulty of individual tasks by repeatedly running multiple agents is costly, while a predicted difficulty score alone provides limited guidance on what support an agent needs. To address these challenges, we propose DARE (Difficulty Analysis for Repair Enhancement), which integrates repair-task difficulty measurement, prediction, feature-group contribution analysis, and task-specific repair support. We define continuous task difficulty as the observed failure rate across multiple coding agents. The DARE difficulty model predicts this difficulty using 151 static features extracted from benchmark artifacts.…

items.title: Non-Pseudo-Arithmetic Hyperbolic 4-Manifolds
items.summary: We give three explicit finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter lattices in dimension four whose adjoint trace fields are not totally real. They are the reflection groups of the Ma--Zheng polytopes $P_{11,6}$, $P_{11,7}$, $P_{11,8}$. The obstruction is contained in two cyclic products of the doubled unit-normal Gram matrix $A=2G$. Those products recover elements $s=\sqrt5$ and $u$ satisfying $$ (s-1)u^2+2(s-3)u+s-7=0. $$ After the embedding $s\mapsto-\sqrt5$, this quadratic has discriminant $8(1-\sqrt5)<0$. The cyclic-product field therefore has a complex place. Vinberg's identification of that field with the adjoint trace field and the Emery--Mila total-reality obstruction imply that the three lattices are not pseudo-arithmetic. Torsion-free orientation-preserving finite-index subgroups yield orientable noncompact finite-volume hyperbolic $4$-manifolds with the same obstruction.…

items.title: ZipDrift: Generating Multimodal Short-Horizon MPC Costs with One-Step Drifting Models
items.summary: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert. We observe that the optimal correction is often multimodal: when a slower opponent can be passed on either side, good corrections of opposite sign coexist, and the expert's choice between them hinges on tiny cost differences. Deterministic regression then averages modes or inherits inconsistent expert tie-breaking. We propose ZipDrift, which trains a one-step drifting generator over MPC cost corrections, tilted toward low closed-loop cost and learned only from cost evaluations of candidate corrections, without differentiating through the optimiser. A few generated candidates are ranked by a learned critic, and the model-based MPC then enforces dynamics and constraints.…

items.title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory stores to retain information across conversations, typically via dense vector embeddings searched with approximate nearest-neighbor methods. The fruit fly's olfactory circuit computes a locality-sensitive hash of sensory input using a strikingly different mechanism - sparse random projection followed by winner-take-all competition - and prior work (Dasgupta et al., 2017) showed this scheme, dubbed FlyHash, preserves neighbor structure better per bit than conventional random-hyperplane hashing (SimHash) on several benchmarks.…
items.tldr: FlyHash, a fruit-fly-inspired locality-sensitive hashing method, improves neighbor-structure preservation over SimHash for large language model agent memory retrieval under matched-bit protocols and genuine relevance labels, but it does not provide practical memory or latency advantages over…

items.title: Unsupervised Neural Operators for Rotating Relativistic Stars: High-Fidelity Equation of State Inference and Pulsar Spin Evolution at Scale
items.summary: Observed populations of rotating neutron stars~(NSs) with millisecond-order periods are powerful probes of fundamental physics. Mass-radius measurements inform poorly constrained properties of degenerate nuclear matter, whereas high-fidelity population synthesis connects unknowns in NS formation and binary evolution to large radio-timing surveys. However, repeated structure calculations are prohibitive due to the computational cost of solving the highly coupled partial differential equations of axisymmetric general relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium that govern rotating NS interiors. Non-rotating calculations or approximate rotational corrections can bias equation of state inference and limit the fidelity of population synthesis in tracing the evolutionary history of progenitors and propagating equation of state uncertainties.…

items.title: Timing is Everything: Inferring Temporal Membership in Continually Updated Models
items.summary: Continual model updating has become a common practice in the deployment of machine learning systems. However, the dynamic training behaviors give rise to new risks not sufficiently addressed by existing studies. In this paper, we present the first systematic study of temporal privacy risk in continually updated deep learning models. We formalize the notion of temporal membership in continually updated models. We then define the temporal membership inference attack, which seeks to infer whether and when individual samples were involved in model training, at both timestamp-level and interval-level granularities. To this end, we propose TMIA, a novel black-box attack that leverages bidirectional LSTMs to infer temporal membership from model outputs observed across successive updates.…

items.title: Closed-Loop Adaptive Sampling on a Generative Ocean Model
items.summary: Adaptive sampling can substantially improve the value of sparse ocean observations by directing mobile robots toward measurements that are most informative for an evolving environment. Recent learned generative ocean models can produce high-resolution forecasts and ensembles at substantially lower computational cost than traditional numerical models, creating an opportunity to use rich predictive forecasts directly in closed-loop robotic sampling. However, these models do not natively provide the explicit uncertainty representations assumed by classical informative-planning methods, and their forecasts often evolve in learned latent spaces rather than directly in physical ocean variables. We develop a multi-robot closed-loop adaptive sampling framework that uses a single learned generative model for forecasting, uncertainty estimation, planning, and measurement assimilation.…

items.title: How Well Can Large Language Models Impersonate Individual Authors? A Comparative Evaluation
items.summary: This study investigates the authorship impersonation capacity of six widely used large language models (LLMs): Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Opus, GPT 5.2, GPT 5.2 Pro, DeepSeek 3.2, and Grok 4.1 Fast. The evaluation was conducted using short product review texts selected to ensure high within author consistency in individual writing style. Two types of in context prompt were designed: a simple prompt with minimal instruction and a complex prompt incorporating explicit stylometric guidance for mimicry. Authorship mimicry was evaluated using a cosine distance based distance to training metric, supplemented by visual analyses of embedding distributions. The results indicate that authorship impersonation remained challenging for most LLMs, with Gemini 3 Pro showing the strongest apparent mimicry performance.…

items.title: BobFlow: Towards Human-Agent Collaborative Data Science Using Dataflows
items.summary: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have established human-agent collaboration as a promising paradigm for data science. Effective collaboration requires a shared computational abstraction that enables agents to reason about processing logic while allowing human analysts to understand, guide, and refine the analysis. Although scripts written in Python or SQL provide precise control, their syntax and execution details can be difficult for analysts to understand and modify. In this paper, we argue that dataflows are an effective abstraction for human-agent collaboration in data science. We introduce BobFlow, a system that combines the dataflow abstraction with the ReAct paradigm. It enables agents to iteratively construct and execute dataflows for data science tasks while allowing analysts to inspect the analysis and provide feedback.…

items.title: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability
items.summary: Hyper-Connections (HC) architectures are increasingly adopted in frontier language models, yet their components remain insufficiently understood and introduce non-negligible training overhead. In this work, we systematically study the HC architecture to understand its components and identify simpler, more efficient designs. We find that learned read/write gating without mixing and unconstrained mixing with fixed gates form two effective interaction groups: either alone achieves performance comparable to mHC. We also identify repeated access to the expanded residual state as a major source of training overhead, even without mixing. These findings lead to SimpleHC, which simplifies the architecture by removing residual mixing and simplifies execution through shared memory access, using the resulting additive structure and shared gate inputs.…
items.tldr: A systematic study of Hyper-Connections architectures identifies the simpler efficient design SimpleHC, which removes residual mixing and uses shared memory access to match mHC performance while adding minimal training overhead and improving stability.

items.title: CARTBench: Rubric-Based Evaluation of Shopping Advice for Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) shopping assistants now recommend products in multi-turn conversations. However, reliable evaluation faces Data scarcity and Difficulty Standardizing Criteria. To address these obstacles, we introduce CARTBench for CART (Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines). For Data scarcity, we curate cases from real commercial shopping needs across 17 retail domains, pairing timestamped dialogue with 1,603 product records. For Difficulty Standardizing Criteria, we develop case-specific rubrics guided by Ideal Response Principles, distilled from excellent replies manually selected from successfully completed orders. These principles also guide Principle-Guided CART Prompting, our structured recommendation strategy. The experimental benchmark contains 1,328 expert-annotated criteria across Core, Excellence, and Safety.…

items.title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) enables multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to scale capacity efficiently, but expert parameters dominate memory even though only a few experts are activated per token: they account for over 90% of model size in modern MoE-MLLMs (e.g., 54 GB out of about 58 GB in BF16 for InternVL3.5-30B-A3B and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B). Expert pruning has emerged as an effective compression strategy, but existing methods aggregate importance uniformly across tokens, ignoring that the same expert may serve different roles for vision versus language processing. To address this, we propose MAEP (Modality-Aware Expert Pruning), a training-free framework that decomposes expert importance by modality in a single forward pass.…
items.tldr: MAEP is a training-free modality-aware expert pruning framework that decomposes expert importance by modality to compress MoE-based multimodal LLMs, reducing memory while maintaining competitive multimodal and text performance.

items.title: Where to Connect? Boosting MLLMs via Dynamic Gated Pathways across ALL ViT and LLM Layers
items.summary: A central yet under-explored question in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) is where to connect---how visual information from a hierarchical vision encoder should be wired into the layer-wise semantics of a large language model. Mainstream MLLMs inject a fixed single-layer visual representation into the LLM and treat all LLM layers as a single consumer, ignoring that different layers demand different visual granularities. Recent multi-layer fusion methods either compress hierarchical features on the encoder side or rely on predefined sparse or hierarchical layer-to-layer connections, and therefore stop short of modeling adaptive cross-layer interactions between the ViT and LLM hierarchies.…
items.tldr: Dynamic Gated Pathways enables all-to-all adaptive routing between every vision transformer layer and every large language model layer, allowing each LLM layer to select visual granularities and improving multimodal performance.

items.title: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting
items.summary: Financial backtests of large language models (LLMs) are meaningful only if the model did not already know the outcomes it is asked to predict. Practitioners guard against this by trusting a vendor's stated knowledge cutoff, by asking the model what it knows, or by instructing it to answer as of a past date. To verify whether any of these safeguards can be trusted, we introduce FinDendro, a benchmark of 2,226 dated U.S. facts from 1999 to 2026, covering monthly macroeconomic series, month-end stock prices and Federal Reserve decisions. Each fact yields four prompts: a value question, Recall and Predict questions that pair each candidate value with a claim of knowing or guessing without a declared date, and a Predict question with a historical declared date. Controls for persistence and dominant outcomes keep chance accuracy near 0.27.…
items.tldr: A benchmark of dated U.S. financial facts shows that large language models often understate their knowledge and that common safeguards cannot reliably certify that historical backtests are free of information leakage.

items.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context. Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent's attention to task-relevant information. Existing token pruning and summarization methods remain constrained by discrete text representations, limiting the achievable compression ratios. In this work, we challenge the prevailing assumption that agents must consume tool observations as explicit text tokens. To this end, we propose Coca-Cola, a continuous latent context compression model for LLM agents. Coca-Cola compresses tool observations into latent tokens and embeds them into the input embedding space of the agent. We further introduce Action-Preserving Training, which aligns the agent's next-action distributions under full and compressed observations.…
items.tldr: A continuous latent context compression model for LLM agents compresses tool observations into latent tokens and uses action-preserving training to reduce token consumption and runtime while improving task performance.

items.title: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing
items.summary: Strong single-turn editing performance does not guarantee reliable multi-turn interaction: as edited outputs are repeatedly reused, small unintended changes can accumulate into severe visual drift. This long-term drift is often mitigated through training on multi-turn data or cross-turn rollouts, potentially altering pretrained priors, or through specialized inference-time mechanisms that are difficult to scale to foundation models. We introduce TailSteer, a final-stage training framework that improves multi-turn robustness while retaining the generative and editing capabilities acquired through earlier training. TailSteer follows a simple principle: keep early denoising dynamics close to those of the base model and concentrate preservation corrections near the trajectory tail, where fine-grained deviations can be suppressed.…
items.tldr: TailSteer, a final-stage training framework, reduces cumulative visual drift in multi-turn editing by keeping early denoising dynamics close to the base model and learning tail-focused preservation corrections from on-policy rollouts, preserving pretrained generative and editing abilities.

items.title: Automated Segmentation of the Hypothalamus: Associations of Age and Socioeconomic Status with Subunit Volumes in Cognitively Healthy Adults
items.summary: Background: The hypothalamus regulates sleep-wake cycles, energy balance, and autonomic and neuroendocrine function, yet its small size and poorly contrasted boundaries have long hindered in vivo volumetry. Deep-learning segmentation now allows the hypothalamus to be divided into functionally meaningful subunits. We examined whether hypothalamic subunit volumes are associated with age and socioeconomic status (SES) in cognitively healthy adults. Methods: From the OASIS-1 cross-sectional dataset (n = 416, 18-96 years), 133 participants with a Clinical Dementia Rating of 0 and complete segmentation output were analysed (33-94 years). A FreeSurfer-based convolutional neural network, run on a cloud virtual machine, segmented five subunits per hemisphere.…

items.title: Brain Decoding from a Deep Neural Network of Visual Memory Reveals the Maturation Trajectory of Memory Systems across Ages 3-7
items.summary: Memories from the first four years of life are largely inaccessible by adulthood, yet these early experiences profoundly shape cognition throughout development. Understanding this phenomenon of infantile amnesia is critical for revealing the mechanisms of early memory development. Here, we developed a new content-based behavioral measure of memory that quantifies how closely children's memory patterns resemble those of adults, which we term the memory maturation score. Using a movie-watching fMRI dataset spanning age 3 to adulthood, we trained a cross-validated model on adults' movie-evoked brain activity to predict adult's propensity to remember each movie snippet, estimated by ResMem, a deep neural network trained to predict visual memorability.…

items.title: SafeLens: A Statistically Controlled Nonlinear Machine Learning Framework for Characterizing Hidden Dynamics in Event-Locked Neural Activity
items.summary: Machine learning has advanced rapidly over the past decade, yet event-locked neural activity is still analyzed predominantly with traditional statistics and linear models. While traditional linear methods provide computationally tractable statistical control for pre-selected features or trial-averaged waveforms, they miss subtle nonlinear and trial-varying neural dynamics. Nonlinear models can capture these complex patterns, but their feature reliance is opaque and notoriously difficult to threshold statistically. We introduce SafeLens (Searchlight Analysis of Fluctuation Events, Leveraging Extensive Null Sampling) to combine the power of nonlinear machine learning with the rigorous false-positive control of traditional statistical inference.…

items.title: The ontogeny of hippocampal spatial memory is supported by postnatal Cajal-Retzius cells
items.summary: The functional capabilities of the adult hippocampus depend on specialized circuits that are established during development. Cajal-Retzius (CR) cells persist in the hippocampus long after their disappearance from the neocortex and contribute to the postnatal maturation of hippocampal circuits, but how this developmental role shapes adult hippocampal function remains unknown. Here, we selectively ablated CR cells from the postnatal hippocampus and examined the consequences for spatial learning, navigation, and CA1 spatial representations. CR-cell ablated animals learned reward locations and adapted to changing task conditions, but learned more slowly and made more errors. Reinforcement-learning models suggest that these behavioral differences reflect less stable internal representations guiding behavior.…

items.title: Vision-language representations link food perception to subjective valuation
items.summary: Subjective values of foods guide dietary decisions. Yet, how the brain computes such values from visual input remains unclear. Here, we show that visual food valuation relies on higher-level conceptual representations captured by a multimodal vision-language deep neural network model. Using food images and human ratings (N = 194 and 200), we found that a vision-language model predicted subjective value more accurately than vision-only models. Representational analyses demonstrated that, compared with the vision-only model, the vision-language model preferentially encoded higher-level food attributes, including perceived healthiness, while encoding less image-level visual information. Multivariate analyses of fMRI data (N = 31) showed that embedding features from both models corresponded to activity patterns along the visual pathways.…

items.title: 2D U-NET Deep Learning Architecture for Atherosclerotic Lesion Segmentation and Quantification
items.summary: Mice are commonly used for experimental atherosclerosis research, and a common procedure involves morphometric analysis of atherosclerotic lesions on Oil Red O-stained cross-sections of the aortic root. However, manual measurement of atherosclerotic lesion sizes on numerous histological sections is tedious and time-consuming. Here, we developed a deep learning model based on convolutional neural network to quantify atherosclerotic lesions in cross-sectioned aortic roots of mice. Microscopy images were taken from cross-sectioned aortic roots of genetically diverse F2 mice derived from BALB/cJ and LP/J Apoe knockout mice and fed 12 weeks of a Western diet. Aortic cross-sections were stained with Oil Red O and hematoxylin and images captured. Atherosclerotic lesions were manually segmented in 2553 images using Zeiss AxioVision.…

items.title: SPaRTA: Spatial Reasoning in Text-to-SQL for Omics Analysis
items.summary: Spatial-omics technologies provide clinicians, pathologists, and biomedical researchers with high-resolution maps of transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic activity within tissues. However, querying these complex datasets often requires specialized computational expertise, limiting their accessibility to domain experts without programming experience. In the current manuscript, we develop SPaRTA (Spatial Reasoning in Text-to-SQL for Omics Analysis), a natural-language interface that translates free-text questions into executable spatial SQL queries over such data.…

items.title: GPBench: A benchmark framework for genomic prediction
items.summary: Genomic prediction (GP) has emerged as a powerful data mining strategy for disease risk assessment and molecular breeding. GP leverages genome-wide genetic variations and phenotypic information through a computational model to estimate genetic potential or disease risk. However, the field of GP still faces several major challenges: (i) dataset bias and insufficient representativeness; (ii) the lack of standardized evaluation protocols and a systematic benchmarking framework; (iii) heavy reliance on empirical expertise for experimental result interpretation, which hinders large-scale and systematic analysis. These issues make it difficult to conduct systematic cross-species evaluation and comparison of GP methods, and their authentic applications. To address these challenges, we established a standardized and extensible GP benchmark framework-GPBench.…

items.title: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit
items.summary: Streaming video understanding requires models to repeatedly decide whether to respond or continue observing. Recently, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has been applied to this setting, with existing approaches emphasizing reward design while retaining a single trajectory-level advantage across turns. Such shared credit can reinforce redundant replies after earlier successes and discourage useful follow-ups after earlier failures. We propose TurnWise, a turn-level GRPO framework that aligns learning with individual streaming decisions. TurnWise addresses the mismatch between trajectory-level feedback and turn-level interaction, promoting informative responses and reducing redundancy.…
items.tldr: TurnWise improves streaming video understanding by assigning turn-level credit and balancing decision weights in group relative policy optimization.

items.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
items.summary: AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Each task requires agents to review the literature, develop a research plan, conduct research and experiments, and produce structured outputs and scientific manuscripts. Combining deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics, FrontierPhysics evaluates whether agents' research is correct and publishable. Across 22 models in 26 configurations, no configuration passes more than 46 of its 168 rollouts.…
items.tldr: FrontierPhysics is an end-to-end benchmark of 56 expert-designed physics tasks that evaluates AI agents on literature review, research planning, experimentation, and manuscript production using deterministic verifiers and expert rubrics.

items.title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL
items.summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has advanced generative model post-training in verifiable domains such as code and mathematics, but evaluating video quality, especially emotional expression, often depends on subjective aesthetics and has no uniquely correct target. Existing approaches typically rely on fixed rewards for visual quality, motion quality, and text alignment that poorly capture emotional intent and can invite reward hacking, while RLHF is difficult to scale and subject to individual aesthetic differences that complicate the calibration of facial, body motion, and chromatic cues across narrative contexts.…

items.title: VA-TDM: A Unified View for Improving Few-Step Diffusion Models by Velocity Adversarial Distillation
items.summary: Few-step distillation offers efficient generation with diffusion and flow models, but preserving quality with only a few sampling steps remains challenging. Distribution-matching methods via score distillation provide a strong foundation, yet they rely on accurately tracking the student's changing distribution. At intermediate generation steps in few-step sampling, student-score estimation can be difficult, and commonly used estimators may describe a different distribution from the one used to update the student. Flow matching allows a more flexible approach to supervision through velocity fields constructed from the student's sampling process. Building on this perspective, we introduce Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD), which uses a learned critic to compare student and teacher fields and turn their disagreement into feedback for learning.…
items.tldr: Velocity Adversarial Distillation and trajectory-aware supervision enable high-quality few-step diffusion and flow generation with state-of-the-art results.

items.title: SleuthVLM: Do We Really Need Audio-in-Video for Omni Video Understanding?
items.summary: Omni models answer questions about videos by jointly processing sampled frames and audio in one turn, with progress driven largely by scaling model size and omni training data. We ask whether a model needs to hear the audio directly at all, and present SleuthVLM, an agent harness built on a VLM that never hears the audio directly: speech will be transcribed into text, and the VLM will sleuth the video on its own without any predefined workflow. On four omni benchmarks with videos up to 90 minutes, SleuthVLM achieves the best average accuracy: 75.0%, 2.6 points above Gemini 3.8 Flash, and it also tops the Video-MME-v2 leaderboard with 77.8%; with an open-source 27B VLM, it beats all open-source omni models.…
items.tldr: SleuthVLM uses a vision-language model with transcribed speech and autonomous video sleuthing to outperform direct audio-hearing omni models on long-video benchmarks, showing that agentic reasoning matters more than auditory input.

items.title: Dissociable Oscillatory Alpha and Aperiodic Neural Dynamics Underlie Atypical Attentional Control in Children With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
items.summary: Children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often have difficulty maintaining goal-directed attention when task-relevant and task-irrelevant information compete for processing resources. The present study investigated whether this difficulty reflects distinct abnormalities in demand-related attentional regulation and distractor-related neural responses. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) signals from 45 children with ADHD and 45 typically developing (TD) children while they performed a visual detection task under low and high visual demands, with simultaneous task-irrelevant standard and deviant sounds. EEG power spectra were parameterized to separate oscillatory alpha activity from aperiodic activity, as putative indices of attentional regulation and cortical excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance, respectively.…

items.title: Concurrent metacognitive evaluation is dissociable from perceptual evidence accumulation in the parietal cortex
items.summary: Adaptive behavior requires not only accumulating evidence toward a choice but also monitoring its reliability in real time. A central question is whether such concurrent uncertainty is read out directly from the circuit that accumulates perceptual evidence, or is computed by a separate process that runs alongside it. We trained two macaques on a perceptual discrimination task in which they could abandon deliberation at any moment and request assistance, so that uncertainty responses were in parallel with, rather than appended to, evidence accumulation. Behaviorally, a race between distinct perceptual and uncertainty accumulators outperformed models in which the opt-out decision was derived from the perceptual decision variable alone.…

items.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Links Group-Specific Plasma Proteomics to Regional Structural Neuroimaging in Alzheimer's Disease
items.summary: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology begins years before clinical symptoms, highlighting the need for scalable biomarkers that capture biological changes across the AD continuum. Broader plasma proteomics may capture systemic processes that vary with disease stage, yet their relationship to AD-related brain neurodegeneration remains unclear. We aimed to identify plasma proteomic signatures across cognitively normal (CN), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and AD and evaluate their neuroanatomical associations. Methods: We analyzed 146 plasma analytes from 565 Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) participants (58 CN, 396 MCI, 111 AD). Group-specific proteomic signatures were identified using pairwise classification models with nested 5*5 cross-validation.…

items.title: Immersion as inference: An active inference account of induced realities and its relation to the two-competitor model
items.summary: Immersive technologies are designed for a single target: the human perceptual system. Engineers of virtual and augmented reality have long recognized that a display does not have to replicate the physical world, it only has to provide the inputs that satisfy the senses at the level at which the brain samples them. This engineering intuition is, in fact, a statement about brain function. Here we develop it into a formal account of immersion within the active inference framework. We treat an induced reality (a virtual, augmented, or mixed reality, but also a book or a daydream) as a candidate generative model that competes with the model of the actual reality for the explanation of a shared sensorium and for the control of action.…

items.title: Differential modulation of the neurocomputational signature of early and late mismatch responses to spoken words by awareness and task relevance
items.summary: Mismatch responses (MMRs), including the mismatch negativity (MMN) and the P3, are a hallmark of the brains capacity to detect unexpected events. They are discussed to be generated by two main processes: adaptation and prediction error (PE). However, MMR research on underlying mechanisms has mostly relied on simple, non-linguistic stimuli such as tones, and it remains unknown how awareness and attentional conditions affect MMRs to auditory verbal stimuli, that, unlike tones, carry lexical-semantic meaning. Here, we conducted a preregistered EEG study that disentangled influences of awareness, general task-relevance of word stimuli, and specific target-relevance of word oddballs on the MMN and P3. In addition, single-trial neurocomputational models were applied to uncover the underlying generative models of the MMRs.…

items.title: Physical sensorimotor contingencies facilitate learning in monkeys
items.summary: Animal studies in neuroscience routinely use virtual tasks that deviate significantly from the animals' natural behavioral repertoire. This choice is often necessary for conducting careful and controlled experimentation. However, this approach raises a fundamental question: do virtual tasks expose neural computations and mechanisms associated with naturalistic tasks? In this study, we explore how naturalistic settings influence learning timescale and generalization behavior in rhesus monkeys. By training animals in a maze-solving task and comparing their behavior across two environments, we observe significant differences. Specifically, we found that a realistic setup using physical objects enabled learning that was orders of magnitude faster than the learning timescale observed in a comparable computerized virtual environment.…

items.title: Contributions of Site Heterogeneity in Multi-site Brain-Phenotype Predictions
items.summary: Machine learning studies of brain-phenotype associations typically summarize accuracy with a single Pearson correlation, yet in harmonized multi-site data this metric is shaped by training-set size, feature and outcome variability, and true effect heterogeneity. We analyzed structural MRI data from the Reproducible Brain Charts consortium. After preprocessing and quality control, 3486 participants from 9 sites were retained. Three training set compositions were used to understand contributions of site heterogeneity after harmonization: within-site (Local), size-downsampled multi-site (Multi-Down), and full multi-site (Multi-Full). Another site-agnostic strategy (Overall) pooled all sites into a single dataset. All strategies included the target site in the training and testing samples. These analyses separate the contribution of the site effect from that of sample size.…

items.title: Neural dynamics become significantly faster and more nonlinear at the peak of information processing
items.summary: The temporal scale at which neural populations preserve stimulus information is often treated as fixed, even though population activity changes rapidly during sensory processing. Whether the information-optimal scale changes within a single stimulus-evoked episode, and what determines its evolution, remains unclear. We developed Integration-Split, a decoding-based framework that estimates the time-varying temporal resolution of population spike trains. Across four visual paradigms and throughout the mouse visual hierarchy, the optimal scale contracted after stimulus onset and subsequently re-expanded. This pattern persisted across stimulus temporal frequencies and was largely absent in a hippocampal control. The optimal scale varied inversely with stimulus decodability, reaching its finest resolution when stimulus identity was most accurately decoded.…

items.title: Linear NeuroPaint: An Efficient Baseline for Cross-Session Neural Alignment and Inpainting
items.summary: Large-scale Neuropixels recordings sample many brain areas, but no single experimental session records every area of interest. NeuroPaint, a transformer-based autoencoder, integrates such recordings by aligning area-specific latent dynamics across sessions and "inpainting" activity in unrecorded areas. Could a linear model, which would be computationally efficient and potentially more interpretable, suffice to achieve this? To address this question, we introduce Linear NeuroPaint, a linear variant of NeuroPaint, and evaluate it on two multi-area Neuropixels datasets. Linear NeuroPaint achieves strong predictive performance on recorded areas, however, it is less accurate than nonlinear models at cross-area inpainting, despite extensive hyperparameter optimization.…

items.title: Decoding Cell-type Specific Gene Regulation with CellReg3D by Integrating DNA Large Language Models and 3D Genome Structure
items.summary: Gene regulation is a core biological mechanism crucial for organismal growth and development. Recent advances in deep learning, coupled with increasing computational resources, have enabled large-scale modelling of gene regulatory processes. While numerous models have been proposed, effectively capturing long-range genomic interactions remains a central challenge. Here, we introduce CellReg3D, a multiscale and multi-modal deep learning framework designed to model cell-type-specific gene regulation by integrating local sequence patterns with long-range genomic interactions. Existing approaches often overlook the contribution of 3D genome architecture and face limitations in combining sequence-based features with chromatin interaction data.…

items.title: Model-Agnostic Decomposition of the Difference in Mean Response Between Two Groups via Game-Theoretic Attribution with Minimum-Switching-Distortion Coupling
items.summary: The difference in mean response between two groups can arise from differences in covariate-response relationships, covariate distributions, or both. We propose a model-agnostic decomposition (MAD) of this difference into structure and composition effects. We formulate a cooperative switching game with a model-switch player and individual covariate-switch players, organized into model and covariate unions. MAD employs the Owen value, whose quotient game yields the aggregate structure and composition effects and whose internal game allocates the aggregate composition effect across covariates, and thereby inherits its fair allocation properties. In the internal game, partial covariate switches create hybrid covariate vectors whose joint distributions are not determined by the group-specific covariate distributions alone.…

items.title: Accelerating antibiotic discovery from Earth's isolated habitats through protein language models and microfluidics
items.summary: The antibiotic potential of Earth's isolated habitat microbiomes remains largely unexplored. Accessing this resource requires reliable prioritization across divergent peptide sequences and efficient experimental validation. Here we present MicroSPEAR, an end-to-end framework for antimicrobial peptide (AMP) discovery integrating SPEAR, a sequence-structure-aware ensemble predictor, with MicroGrad, a microfluidic testing platform. SPEAR generalized to low-homology peptides and prioritized potent candidates despite training on binary activity labels. MicroGrad simplified liquid handling and shortened susceptibility testing from approximately 18 h to 4 h. Applied to a catalogue derived from 4,480 metagenomes spanning 15 isolated habitat types, SPEAR identified 383,027 non-redundant candidate AMPs, 63.1% of which lacked detectable homologues in reference databases.…

items.title: scPCIP: cross-species annotation of plant cell types with conserved gene programs
items.summary: Single-cell atlases now cover many plant species and organs, yet their cell types are still annotated with marker genes that often fail to transfer between species. Here we show that plant cell identities are captured by gene programs conserved across species. We learned programs for root, leaf, flower and seed cell types on ortholog groups from 112,905 author-labelled cells and implemented them in scPCIP, which annotates cells of species absent from training without a reference. Across 26 held-out datasets, scPCIP outperformed marker-based and plant deep-learning methods, matched supervised classifiers trained on the same atlas and transferred, at lower accuracy, to an independent study; its programs followed tissue position in spatial transcriptomes.…

items.title: PaleoRigor: a bounded research agent with a reproducible evidence trail for paleomicrobiome data processing
items.summary: Background: Ancient microbial evidence informs research on past health, diet, and environments, but its scarcity and susceptibility to contamination demand care in selecting and processing data. Language models can now turn a research request into an analysis plan, but an unconstrained planner may reference files that do not exist, apply operations a format forbids, or answer a question the data cannot settle. A planner used on such evidence therefore needs to be bounded, and its decisions recoverable afterwards. Results: We developed PaleoRigor around three commitments. Agent: a language model plans the analysis.…

items.title: Neural RNA splicing models rely on reading frame information unavailable to the splicing machinery
items.summary: Deep neural networks can accurately predict RNA splice sites from genomic sequence, but whether they do so by simulating the natural splicing process is unclear. We evaluate this question by examining mutations that should not have a strong effect on splicing, but are correlated with it in the human genome. We focus specifically on mutations that affect frame alignment because this is known to be relevant to machinery that operates spatially and temporally separately from the splicing machinery. We find that predictions made by commonly-used neural tools are impacted far more by deletions or mutations that alter translational reading frame, producing in-frame stop codons, than by those that preserve reading frame. This dependence on reading frame causes these models to systematically miss many poison exons, a clinically relevant category of exons where reading frame is disrupted.…

items.title: Disentangling Context-Specific Alzheimer's Disease Progression Signatures through an Explainable AI Framework
items.summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression involves stage-dependent transcriptional changes that are often masked by dominant cellular and biological variation. Here, we present ADVISE (Alzheimer's Disease Variational Isolation of Signal Embeddings), an interpretable deep generative framework designed to disentangle Braak stage-associated transcriptional signals from background biological variation through separate latent representations. Using explainable AI, ADVISE prioritizes genes and pathways contributing to the disease-specific representation.…

items.title: CloneVI: A deep generative model for deciphering the relationships between cell state and mitochondrial genotype
items.summary: Cellular diversity arises from both genetic lineages and non-genetic regulation of cell states, and knowing which cell states are tied to lineages is central to understanding how clones shape disease. Single-cell multi-omics technologies measure mitochondrial DNA mutations together with gene expression or chromatin accessibility in the same cells, but clones are usually inferred from mutations alone, making such clones difficult to identify. We developed CloneVI, a deep generative model that infers clonal structure from a latent cell state derived from gene expression or chromatin accessibility. It estimates the clonal probability of each cell from this cell state, together with the allele frequency of each clone by reconstructing the observed mutation counts. In simulated data, CloneVI recovered the ground-truth clonal structure in both single-clone and mixed-clone cell populations.…

items.title: Omics-scale decoding of protein N-glycosylation using protein language model embeddings
items.summary: Protein language models (pLMs) learn rich sequence semantics from vast volume of protein sequences, yet the information encoded in their high-dimensional embeddings remains largely a black box, posing an interpretability challenge. Here we show that semantic features learned by pLMs can be decoded to reveal biologically meaningful signals using coevolutionary analysis without downstream supervised-training. Building on this insight, we developed MaskNGly, a zero-shot framework that identifies protein N-glycosylation sites directly from PLM-embeddings while achieving performance comparable to state-of-the-art supervised predictors. MaskNGly is computationally efficient and intrinsically transferable, enabling omics-scale characterization of protein glycosylation landscape.…

items.title: MicrobeRT: A Framework and Suite of Fine-tuned Language Models for Genomic Sequences
items.summary: Accurate and reproducible metagenomic analysis is essential for effective infectious disease surveillance. Targeted diagnostics such as culturing, antigen assays, and multiplex PCR panels identify only predefined organisms and can fail to identify atypical or novel infections. Shotgun metagenomics offers hypothesis-free detection, but adoption is limited by workflow complexity, dependence on mutable reference databases, and high computational cost. To combat these challenges, we introduce MicrobeRT, an integrated suite of genomic language models fine-tuned to classify metagenomic sequencing reads across three tasks: (i) species level taxonomic identification, (ii) antibiotic resistance gene detection, and (iii) pathogenicity assessment.…

items.title: Rho: A Purpose-Driven Workspace for Human-AI Collaborative Analysis
items.summary: Agent-assisted bioinformatics has moved the bottleneck from computing a result to judging it: whether a comparison answers the intended question, on which unit of replication, at which version of the input, and what would change the conclusion. These judgments need materials that are usually scattered across conversations, notebooks, figures, run logs and notes, while the agent's context is a transcript rather than the structure the researcher is actually reading. We present Rho, a human--AI collaborative analysis environment that organizes materials by the current scientific purpose: it selects or obtains the materials a judgment needs, declares the relations they serve, composes operable views, and makes this organization a shared state that is at once the researcher's reading interface and the agent's continuation context.…

items.title: All-Atom Structure Tokenizer: AtomLM-9b for Biomolecular Structure Prediction
items.summary: We develop an All-atom Structure Tokenizer that compresses biomolecular geometry into discrete structural tokens and achieves high-accuracy all-atom reconstruction. A hierarchical geometric encoder and finite scalar quantization map chemical units to a shared vocabulary of 8,192 tokens, while a joint coordinate de-tokenizer reconstructs backbone, side-chain, nucleic-acid, and ligand heavy atoms. The tokenizer achieves all-atom lDDT scores of 0.832 and 0.835 on CASP14 and CASP15, respectively. Building on this tokenizer, we train AtomLM-9b, an autoregressive language model based on Qwen3.5-9B that predicts structural tokens from molecular identities and connectivity and decodes them into complete atomic structures.…

items.title: XAMPGen: An Interpretable SI Pipeline For Novel Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery
items.summary: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are short peptides with a broad spectrum of activity against bacterial pathogens, representing a promising avenue for combating the growing threat of antibiotic resistance. This study focuses on two main components: 1) generating novel AMPs with desired properties using generative SI (GenSI) and 2) utilizing explainable SI (XSI) methods to validate the GenSI model and derive biological insights. In this work, we fine-tuned ProGen, a decoder-only protein language model, on known AMPs to generate novel peptide sequences with strong antimicrobial properties. To advance the interpretability and reliability of the generative model, we applied Explainable SI (XSI) techniques. Specifically, we used a probing classifier and a regressor to identify cornerstone layers that encode functionally critical information.…

items.title: Where single-cell foundation models help: a benchmark of annotation, perturbation and regulatory inference against simple baselines
items.summary: Single-cell foundation models (FMs) are proposed as general tools for cell-type annotation, in silico perturbation and gene-regulatory-network (GRN) inference. To identify where they add value, we benchmarked five FMs (scGPT, Geneformer V1 and V2, Nicheformer, scFoundation), CellOracle, supervised perturbation models including STATE, and task-matched simple baselines on the same data, from K562 Perturb-seq screens and primary cells to healthy-donor and isogenic leukodystrophy brain organoids, a public organoid CRISPR screen and lung cancer biopsies. FMs were most useful when labels had to be transferred across species: from human to mouse lung, Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy and Geneformer V2 and scFoundation about 0.90, against 0.68 for the best baseline.…

items.title: Error-Controlled Discovery of Protein Interactions via Conformal Calibration
items.summary: Protein language models (PLMs) are powerful predictors of protein interactions, but strong benchmark performance does not ensure reliable discoveries. We introduce PPI-Caliper, a model-agnostic framework that adapts conformal calibration to select interactions at user-specified false discovery rate (FDR) levels using held-out labels without retraining the predictor. Across five species, two PLM-based predictors, and two human training-data versions for each predictor, PPI-Caliper keeps empirical FDR at or below the target level under in-distribution calibration. Under distribution shift, transferred thresholds tend to become conservative when predictive performance improves, but can fail to control FDR when performance deteriorates.…

items.title: Autonomous generalizability auditing of scientific foundation models
items.summary: Determining where scientific foundation models generalize beyond their development data is essential for reliable use, but aggregate benchmarks obscure performance limits and rigorous audits are difficult to conduct routinely. Here, we introduce AutoSPECTRA, a coding-agent protocol for systematic generalizability auditing. To inform its design, we reviewed 38 studies across five biological domains and evaluated coding agents, which generated hypotheses and empirical analyses but applied inconsistent standards for judging evidence. We then structured AutoSPECTRA around measurable generalization axes, prespecified analyses, controlled comparisons and independent confirmation.…

items.title: CARTnet: Template-guided B-cell Epitope Prediction with Contact-aware Attention
items.summary: B-cell epitope prediction remains challenging due to the limited availability of experimentally characterized data and the incomplete understanding of antibody-antigen recognition. Here, we present CARTnet, a novel contact-aware deep learning framework that integrates multimodal features and template-derived epitope information. CARTnet demonstrated superior performance when compared to the existing state-of-the-art methods across most evaluation metrics on both the internal and external test datasets. In particular, CARTnet achieved an AUPRC of 0.243 on the internal test set, compared with 0.220 for DiscoTope-3, 0.140 for BepiPred-2, and 0.198 for BepiPred-3.…

items.title: Cross-cancer knowledge transfer for lymph node metastasis prediction: Applicability of an axillary lymph node-based deep learning model
items.summary: Evaluation of lymph node (LN) metastasis is critical for cancer staging and treatment planning. Since radiologic hallmarks of metastatic LNs are shared across primary cancers, a computed tomography (CT)-based deep learning (DL) classifier developed from one anatomy may transfer to others. This study built a DenseNet-121 ensemble model using clinical-implication-applied preprocessing and evaluated its cross-anatomical generalizability to LNs from diverse primary cancers. A DenseNet-121 ensemble model combining fixed-size cropping (FSC) and adjustable square cropping (ASC) was trained from ImageNet initialization on an axillary lymph node (ALN) dataset (n = 1,128 from 523 breast cancer patients). The model utilized clinical-implication-applied perinodal cropping with bicubic filtering and standardized resizing.…

items.title: Photographic age gap is associated with frailty and predicts survival in laboratory mice
items.summary: Ageing studies in mice need biomarkers that are cheap, non-invasive and repeatable. We asked how much of a mouse's age can be read from an ordinary photograph, and whether the part that cannot be explained by age carries biological information. We assembled 2,846 photographs of 1,292 mice (four strains, 1 to 34 months old) from seven facilities and predicted age with a frozen self-supervised vision model (DINOv2) and a ridge regression, always tested on facilities the model had never seen. Absolute age transferred poorly between facilities (median absolute error 138 days), because each facility's photographs carried an offset.…

items.title: Roost: Avian Influenza Host Genomics Resource
items.summary: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) causes mass mortality in poultry and wildlife, and puts already threatened species at further risk. Understanding differences in host susceptibility requires evidence currently scattered across publications, surveillance reports and genomic resources. We present Roost, a web resource that brings together more than 1,300 publications and reports, surveillance detections, and a catalogue of over 2,000 avian genome assemblies. Large language model-assisted literature analysis and comparative genomics link species, genes and molecular mechanisms to their supporting evidence. Around 51% of species with HPAI detections are not represented in the analysed corpus. Research concentrates on poultry, model organisms, and a small set of immune pathways.…

items.title: Predicting single-molecule chromatin distribution from DNA sequence
items.summary: Genome regulation unfolds through dynamic and stochastic single-molecule events. Deep learning models that read gene regulatory activities from DNA sequences have markedly advanced our ability to predict cell-population-level averages. However, they cannot capture the full spectrum of heterogeneity and dynamics at the single-molecule level, which directly reflect the underlying mechanisms of genome regulation. Here, we introduce a sequence-to-distribution (S2d) framework that directly models the entire probabilistic distribution of single-molecule chromatin states from DNA sequence alone. We used this framework to train Mola, a model of single-molecule chromatin accessibility. We harness Mola to investigate sequence-based regulatory code and mechanisms for multiple aspects of chromatin regulation at the single-molecule level.…

items.title: DB-ATRG: The Density and BI-RADS-Aware Triage and Automatic Report Generation System for Mammography
items.summary: Background: The growing volume of mammography screenings has created severe radiologist shortages, while standard First-In, First-Out (FIFO) reading queues fail to prioritize urgent or complex cases, delaying critical diagnoses.
