Results show that neither method is universally best: on multiple-choice QA (MedQA and EMS-MCQA), SwS generally performs better, with general-purpose models benefiting most; notably, Qwen3.5-4B improves by up to 44.8% over its zero-shot baseline on MedQA. In contrast, medical-domain models show smaller or even negative gains on MCQs.…

items.title: Camera Radar LiDAR Fusion via Point-Cloud Projection for Multi-Task Learning
items.summary: Autonomous vehicles require robust perception systems to operate safely under diverse environmental conditions. While cameras provide high-resolution visual data, their performance significantly degrades in low-light and adverse weather. High Definition (HD) radar offers superior reliability and angular resolution under such conditions but lacks rich visual feature recognition. LiDAR, though expensive, delivers highly precise distance measurements and dense point clouds. Each sensor exhibits unique trade-offs, necessitating the development of advanced sensor fusion algorithms to harness complementary strengths while minimizing computational complexity and maintaining accuracy. In this study, the proposed fusion architecture performs early fusion by combining camera images with perspective-view point cloud data from HD radar and LiDAR sensors.…

items.title: FlowBench: Counterfactual Imagination Training for Spatial Intelligence
items.summary: Humans imagine scene changes under hypothetical motions, an ability central to spatial reasoning and robotic planning. However, this capability remains underexplored in vision-language models and world models. We formalize this capability as Counterfactual Spatial Imagination (CSI) and introduce FlowBench, a resource for training and evaluating both, with 428K training examples spanning simulated and real-world scenes, household environments and tabletop manipulation, and diverse question types. A scalable, fully automatic pipeline pairs each hypothetical motion with spatial questions and, in simulation, exact outcome frames and optical flow.…

items.title: Modular and Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbors Search with Vectorium and kANNolo
items.summary: Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN) search over neural embeddings powers modern retrieval systems such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Embeddings come in three representations (dense, sparse and multi-vector), and efficient search combines an index structure, a similarity function and a quantization scheme. Existing libraries fix one combination, hard-code each one separately, or factor only one side of the problem, and none covers all three representations. We present Vectorium and kANNolo, two open-source Rust libraries that split this design space into a data-management layer and an indexing layer. Vectorium abstracts the vector, the distance function, the quantizer and the dataset independently, and provides 11 encoders, from 32-bit floats to sub-bit codes.…

items.title: Tropical Cyclone-Following Dataset for Limited-Area Machine Learning Applications
items.summary: This work presents a lightweight dataset of tropical cyclone (TC)-following meteorological variables to facilitate the development and application of machine learning (ML) methods in TC research. Using outputs from our previous climate downscaling and idealized simulations, the dataset is constructed as multichannel video sequences that track TC centers throughout their lifetimes. To demonstrate the dataset utility, we present an application in which a regional ML model is trained to predict TC intensity with explicit incorporation of lateral boundary conditions. Our results highlight the importance of lateral boundary information for predicting TC intensity with ML models inside a limited-area domain, underscoring the need to properly account for lateral boundaries when developing regional ML models for TC intensity forecast.

items.title: Handling JAX
items.summary: Languages that target hardware accelerators typically expose a restricted, first-order core without recursion or first-class functions, leaving programmers without a principled way to express computational effects. This paper presents a technique for compiling effect handlers to such a constrained target. We introduce a novel translation that statically eliminates effect handlers, and prove that it preserves both typing and semantics. Moreover, we address the challenges of integrating effect handlers with structured control flow, where continuations cannot be constructed statically. The calculus and all our results are fully mechanized in the Lean 4 proof assistant. Finally, we implement our design as a library for JAX, a Python domain-specific language for accelerator programming, and demonstrate its expressiveness through practical case studies.

items.title: When Latent Dynamics Meet Data Assimilation: A Benchmark of Koopman-Type Representations
items.summary: Koopman representations describe nonlinear dynamics through linear evolution in a transformed space, offering an attractive framework for their linear simplicity and generality. Yet these advantages do not necessarily translate into improved performance in deep latent data assimilation (LDA). We systematically compare seven representative methods and structural baselines across five systems spanning approximately periodic to strongly chaotic dynamics and a broad range of state dimensions. We evaluate forecast and assimilation accuracy, physical state recovery, latent-trajectory behavior, and dynamical consistency, and assess Gaussian error assumptions, objective convexity, and uniqueness of analysis solutions. Our results reveal a trade-off between representational flexibility and optimization tractability.…

items.title: Fly Whiskers Meet LiDAR: Robust Navigation under Sensor Failure
items.summary: We extend FLYNN, a leaky integrator recurrent network wired on the Drosophila melanogaster connectome, with a 32-ray 2D LiDAR interface that requires no learned fusion layer beyond a scalar input gain. A 270 degree frontal scan at 8 m range is injected as inverted proximity into the 37 BM Vib head-bristle neurons. Across 24 paired comparisons in a four- state vision matrix with LiDAR on or off, FLYNN-LiDAR has 17 significant wins, 5 nonsignificant comparisons, and 2 significant losses against three LiDAR-capable baselines. Both losses are to MobileNet with the left eye off. With full vision, FLYNN- LiDAR reaches 96.6% success. Under total vision loss, the scan raises success from 45.2% to 64.6%; the baselines reach 44.6% to 56.6% with the scan on.…

items.title: Self-Consistent Neural Control: Learning Trajectories for Implicit Equilibrium
items.summary: One big challenge in physical AI is interacting with systems whose states are defined by implicit equilibrium. Learning in these systems is difficult because their responses can be multistable, path-dependent, and sensitive over long horizons. Adjoint learning provides an efficient way to optimize trajectories without unrolling iterative equilibrium solvers, but its gradient relies on the frozen-tangent approximation, which neglects higher-order sensitivity terms and can become inaccurate when the local equilibrium varies rapidly. In this work, we introduce Self-Consistent Neural Control (SCNC), optimizing trajectories along which sensitivity variations are explicitly controlled. We derive a mathematical bound on the resulting gradient error and develop a practical finite-difference approximation.…

items.title: Lemmas and Conjectures in Spectral Graph Theory
items.summary: The corpus of Elie Duhamel and Tristan Cazenave~\cite{dc} contains $305{,}755$ automatically generated conjectures relating spectral and metric invariants of connected graphs. A pipeline generated with Claude Code (numerical refutation, proof by the SMT solver \textsf{z3} from a library of lemmas, discovery of new lemmas, formalisation in \lean~4/Mathlib) refuted $162{,}964$ conjectures and proved $117{,}390$ without any unproved hypothesis, of which $79{,}505$ are verified end to end in \lean{} for every connected graph. This document collects, with proofs written for mathematicians, the most interesting lemmas that were discovered and proved, the ten most useful lemmas, the ten hardest theorems, simpler proofs of known results (Bollobás--Erdős, Yang--Lu), and the unrefuted conjectures that we find most interesting. All the proofs are gathered in an archive

items.summary: automatic-speech-recognition / transformers

items.title: Dr. No: Feature Steering for Abstention in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Large foundation models often answer even when the available visual or textual evidence is insufficient to support a reliable conclusion. This failure to abstain makes them hard to trust in high-stakes or information-seeking settings, where a confident but unsupported answer can be worse than no answer at all. It also raises a natural question: can the internal mechanisms behind this behaviour be identified and controlled at inference time? We present Dr. No, a feature-steering approach that mines sparse autoencoder (SAE) features associated with abstention and commitment, then modulates a small set of them during the prefill pass, without retraining the base model. Dr. No is evaluated on LLaVA-1.6 Mistral 7B across multimodal abstention benchmarks, including UNK-VQA and MM-UPD, and additionally benchmarked on language reasoning tasks using Qwen3.5-2B on AbstentionBench subsets.…

items.title: Performance, Scalability and Maintenance: An Experimental Study of RPA vs. Autonomous Agents in the Healthcare Domain
items.summary: Healthcare information systems are fragmented, and retrieving data from legacy web portals is a recurrent need. Robotic Process Automation (RPA) is deterministic but sensitive to interface changes, whereas autonomous agents based on large language models (Agent Process Automation, APA) promise adaptability at a higher computational cost. Following Design Science Research, we developed and compared an RPA solution (Playwright) and an APA solution (browser-use, LangGraph and Gemini 2.5 Flash-lite) to retrieve mammography and breast ultrasound reports from a laboratory portal, treating reports solely as informational artifacts. Across two rounds (T and T+7), RPA reached 98.90% accuracy and 98.27% F1-score versus 96.49% and 94.48% for APA, was about 13 times faster (16.07 s vs. 207.21 s per patient) and cost about six times less per report (USD 0.030 vs. 0.187).…
authors: Ana Paula Wernz da Cunha Müller

items.title: High-fidelity quantum gate learning via physics-informed neural networks
items.summary: We propose a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approach for high-fidelity quantum gate learning in both one- and two-qubit systems. We train a PINN using the time-dependent Schrödinger equation, where smooth control fields with fixed boundary conditions are obtained by minimizing a loss function that considers model dynamics, gate error, physical constraints, regularization terms, and multiple initial conditions. Training considers pairs of mutually unbiased bases, while independent validation combines Haar-random input states with the average gate fidelity. Unitary simulations yield an average gate infidelity of $8.49\times10^{-8}$ for Hadamard and values between $3.39\times10^{-7}$ and $4.96\times10^{-6}$ for controlled-NOT under $XX$, $YY$, and $ZZ$ interactions.…

items.title: Luciferutts/partspilot
items.summary: 面向中小汽配制造企业的 AI 业务工作台：真实产品目录、潜客发现与证据审核、RAG 资料问答、多轮询盘、人工交接和报价跟进，附可复现的分层评测。

items.title: PianoBench: Evaluating Musical Perception and Reasoning in Language Models
items.summary: Multimodal language models continue to improve on broad music understanding benchmarks, but which musical features can they perceive and reason about? We investigate this question by introducing PianoBench, a benchmark that tasks language models with reasoning about musical performances across congruent acoustic and symbolic input representations. PianoBench is derived from our new multimodal, training-scale dataset comprising more than 20,000 hours of interleaved transcripts of music and spoken musical commentary from instructional piano videos. Open-weight audio-language models achieve at most 52.8% accuracy on PianoBench, and at best only modestly outperform their accuracy on a no-audio control.…

items.title: El Agente Fármaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery
items.summary: Computational drug discovery offers a growing range of tools for proposing and evaluating molecules, but combining them and deciding what to do next still requires substantial expert effort. Here, we introduce El Agente Fármaco, an AI scientist that uses modern large language model (LLM) technology to turn discovery goals expressed in everyday language into complex, scalable computational screening workflows. The agentic harness selects scientific tools, reviews their results, and adjusts subsequent steps to the target and the user's objectives. Our approach centers on a shared scientific memory: Fármaco Atlas, which stores molecules, structures, and results together with their provenance -- a record of how they were obtained. The agent uses targeted database queries to retrieve the evidence needed for each decision.…

items.title: Rethinking Next-Visit Diagnosis Prediction Beyond Aggregate Metrics: Retrieval--Memory Multi-Agent Adjudication
items.summary: Next-visit diagnosis prediction forecasts the diagnoses documented at a patient's next encounter, turning retrospective electronic health records into prospective clinical prediction. However, conventional aggregate evaluation obscures its multifaceted nature: distributionally, models must handle variable-size diagnosis sets and long-tailed labels; temporally, they must distinguish persistent, newly recorded, and recurrent diagnoses; and both vary with observed history depth. We introduce an evaluation framework along these dimensions and apply it to rule-based heuristics, LLM-based prompting, retrieval, memory, and multi-agent approaches.…

items.title: AIRoA-0: Long-Horizon, Precise, Cross-Embodiment Manipulation from Handheld Data
items.summary: AIRoA-0 (A-0) is a bimanual manipulation system learned from 16,151 hours of handheld demonstrations, with no robot data collected at any stage. The demonstrations are recorded with YUBI, our open-source handheld gripper, which lets people record manipulation data anywhere with no robot present. From a single instruction, A-0 sorts more than a dozen small parts into their numbered cells and changes the mop pads and brush of a robot vacuum; among other tasks, it unzips a pencil case and folds a towel. It performs these tasks using only a camera on each wrist, with no head or scene camera, at a site where none of its training data was recorded. Across the ten tasks of our evaluation, it averages a success rate of 78%, against 27% for the strongest of four other vision-language-action models post-trained on the same task demonstrations.…

items.title: BEND 2.0: Benchmarking the Capabilities Needed to Design DNA
items.summary: Genomic foundation models are increasingly used to propose DNA sequences and edits. But successful design requires capabilities that current benchmarks do not measure. Here we introduce BEND 2.0 (BENchmark for DNA language models), which tests how well models predict the effects of DNA changes and whether these predictions can guide sequence design. Across eight tasks built on five experimental datasets, we find that model choice and how representations are accessed both affect performance. Linear readouts fitted to frozen representations can match or exceed models' native outputs, and functional post-training substantially improves the models' capabilities. Linear readouts transfer well across experimental assays and genes, suggesting that models capture functional patterns beyond the data used to fit individual predictors.…
items.tldr: BEND 2.0 evaluates DNA language models on predicting mutation effects and guiding sequence design, revealing that linear readouts and post-training improve performance but context-specific and multi-objective design remain challenging.

items.title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
items.summary: Sensorized human demonstrations offer scalable data for mobile manipulation, but embodiment differences complicate policy learning. We present Pixel-UMI, a pipeline for learning environment-aware whole-body policies from human data. We first introduce Environment-Aware Retargeting (EAR), which combines reconstructed scene geometry with demonstrated head and gripper trajectories to determine robot posture and generate collision-aware joint and base targets. Delay-calibrated action assignment converts these trajectories into actions. However, kinematic differences can leave residual pose errors, creating viewpoint mismatches between human demonstrations and robot observations. We therefore introduce Retargeting-Error-Aware Masking (REAM), which uses these errors during training to reduce reliance on mismatched views at deployment.…

items.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
items.summary: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution.…

items.title: From Natural Language to Exact Cover: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Zebra Puzzles
items.summary: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation has substantially improved the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on complex reasoning tasks, including code generation, data analysis, and exam-style question answering. Despite these advances, purely neural LLMs continue to struggle with elementary logical reasoning problems and lack the determinism, soundness, and reliability characteristic of symbolic reasoning systems. Conversely, classical symbolic methods such as SAT solving and exact cover guarantee correctness and completeness, but require problems to be expressed in highly specialized formal encodings, limiting their applicability to natural language inputs. In this work, we present a synergistic neuro-symbolic framework that bridges this gap by combining neural semantic parsing with deterministic exact cover reasoning.…

items.title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
items.summary: Muon has recently emerged as a promising optimizer for pretraining large language models, offering a speedup over AdamW in minimizing pretraining loss. However, it remains unclear whether Muon's advantage persists after fine-tuning. In this paper, we study the downstream behavior of Muon and AdamW and uncover a surprising trend: beyond a sufficiently large pretraining data budget, AdamW outperforms Muon after fine-tuning. Moreover, as model size increases, AdamW overtakes Muon at progressively smaller pretraining token-parameter ratios. To explain this reversal, we view fine-tuning as a perturbation of the outputs and introduce the margin-to-spread ratio, which measures how far the correct logit lies above the wrong ones relative to how widely the wrong logits are spread.…

items.title: Not All Reasoning Generalizes: A Case Study on Learning Generalizable Reasoning Strategies in RLVR
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) can enable generalizable improvement for large language model (LLM) reasoning. This paper studies how to incentivize such generalization via reasoning strategies. We study this question with a controllable equation-solving framework: finding multiple inputs x for equations f(x)=y, where f is a non-bijective string function. This setting makes reasoning strategies observable while supporting a clear definition of easy-to-hard out-of-distribution (OOD) shifts, e.g., more solutions, longer y, etc. We uncover a subtle RLVR failure: it teaches the model to solve in-distribution tasks with high accuracy and structured step-by-step derivation, yet under OOD shifts, the same model abandons derivation and collapses to ineffective brute-force enumeration, causing sharp accuracy drops.…

items.title: Isekai3D SDG: A Platform for Diverse Synthetic Gameplay Visual Data
items.summary: We present Isekai3D Synthetic Data Generation (SDG), a platform for simulating and capturing synthetic 3D gameplay for research in vision and world models, neural graphics, gameplay agents, and other applications. The platform combines reusable environment and character assets with Unreal Engine plugins in a two-stage workflow. First, world simulation generates gameplay while recording the world state, character movements, actions, and camera tracks needed for replay. Second, the recorded simulation is replayed to capture selected outputs, such as rendered video, images, and depth maps, at a specified resolution and frame rate under selected rendering and camera configurations. Separating simulation from capture allows the same recorded gameplay to produce multiple output variants without repeating the original simulation.…

items.title: Thought-deciphering via hierarchical EEG-to-text alignment
items.summary: Non-invasive brain-to-text interfaces offer alternative communication pathways for people with communication disabilities. However, sentence-level decoding from electroencephalography (EEG) remains challenging. We propose a hierarchical EEG-text alignment framework that retrieves sentences by progressively decoding coarse-grained semantic information and fine-grained sentence representations. We hypothesize that broader semantic context can be more reliably captured from EEG than individual sentences. Accordingly, EEG representations are first aligned with semantic classes, followed by sentence retrieval within the predicted class. Among over 2,000 unique text samples, our approach achieves average top-5 and top-10 retrieval accuracies of 62.6\% $\pm$ 1.0\% and 83.5\% $\pm$ 1.0\%, respectively, compared with 50.3\% $\pm$ 2.3\% and 68.3\% $\pm$ 2.0\% for direct EEG-sentence alignment.…

items.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
items.summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) hold promise for zero-shot video task-progress estimation in robot learning, yet existing frameworks frequently suffer from confirmation bias, hallucinating progress in failed executions due to implicit success assumptions or relative temporal ranking designs. Naive prompting of frontier models collapses into a binary success detector that fails to capture nuanced, non-linear progress and failures. While post-training approaches can mitigate this through explicit training, they demand expensive real-world robotics data and require computationally intensive post-training for every individual base model. To resolve these limitations, we introduce D&A (Describe & Assess): our approach decouples progress estimation into an objective, task-grounded textual description of scene dynamics followed by an assessment phase using explicit rubrics.…

items.title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) show growing promise for scientific discovery, yet basic questions remain about what enables reliable discovery. How can we trace the scientific discovery capacity of LLMs to their training data? We study this question as one of missing probability mass and develop a theoretical account in which monofacts-the facts observed once during training-set the discovery capacity. In materials science and regulatory genomics, we directly manipulate monofact rates in training sets and find that more monofacts consistently yield more discoveries across two open-weight model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets. Further experiments show the relationship cannot be explained by training-set diversity alone and can transfer across scientific domains when paired with in-domain data.…

items.title: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches
items.summary: Increased computing power has transformed computational science and improved predictive capabilities for complex systems, but many phenomena still exceed current simulation capabilities or require rapid evaluations for fast design iterations. Closure models address this challenge by approximating unresolved effects in reduced or incomplete dynamical systems. Data-driven closures offer a flexible mechanism for improving model accuracy and applicability, but approaches that embed the closure within a computational model for construction and training phases can be computationally expensive and cause numerical instabilities in the computational model during training. To avoid the challenges posed by embedded approaches, staged approaches to closure-model learning have been developed. The first stage uses data assimilation to infer state and closure trajectories from observations.…

items.title: Automatic Generation of Novel Highly-Functional Molecular Sequences
items.summary: While multiple methods now exist to generate functional sequence variants from existing annotated examples, it is unclear how well such methods can be used to generate sequences that exceed the functionality of those contained in the example set. Using two complete fitness landscapes, we quantify how effectively generative tools can search sequence space and find rare, novel, highly functional sequences, focusing on variational auto-encoders and information-theoretic methods. We find that an information-theoretic method that does not require training and runs significantly faster than standard Machine-Learning/Artificial Intelligence (ML/AI) methods also is significantly more effective in finding rare highly-functional sequences.…

items.title: Reviso: Not All Visual Evidence Deserves Equal Attention in Video Captioning
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate detailed video captions, yet they may overemphasize minor details while overlooking essential context and key events. We argue that not all visual evidence deserves equal attention, as the importance of visual information depends on the content of each video. Motivated by this observation, we propose Reviso, an agentic video captioning framework that learns what to observe and how to gather relevant visual evidence. From a low-frame-rate global preview, Reviso constructs a hierarchical Context--Focus--Points (CFP) observation plan that identifies the video context, prioritizes key aspects, and defines concrete observation targets and corresponding tools. Guided by this plan, Reviso performs goal-directed active perception by selectively revisiting temporal segments and combining tools for fine-grained inspection.…
items.tldr: Reviso is an agentic video captioning framework that learns to prioritize key visual evidence through hierarchical planning and active perception, improving caption quality and downstream video understanding.

items.title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
items.summary: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions.…

items.title: Four Bridges: Measuring Deception Propensity in a Multi-Agent Game
items.summary: AI agents are increasingly deployed in settings where they interact and coordinate with other agents, yet honesty is mostly measured in single-turn, single-agent benchmarks that pressure the model to deceive. We study deception that emerges in multi-agent interaction without any instruction to deceive. We introduce Kradle, a platform for evaluating AI models, and Four Bridges, an information asymmetry game in which four agents distribute across four rooms: one is the death room, the others hold food worth more if not shared. One agent, the informed agent, knows which room is the death room and can withhold or disclose that information. We evaluate eight frontier models as the informed agent. Deceptive behavior appears in every model and in 73% of all runs (6% to 100% per model), and does not decrease with capability tier within a model family.…

items.title: Structured Visual Landscape: Generating Preferred Representations in Biological and Artificial Neural Networks
items.summary: Understanding how neurons respond to visual stimulus is an important question in both deep learning and neuroscience. It has significant implications for enhancing the interpretability of black-box artificial neural networks and for understanding the visual representation in the human brain. We propose a structured visual representations landscape and design an activation-based prior that allows us to effectively regularize the landscape with activations from brain regions or neural network units. Our model Vis-Lens integrates a variational autoencoder and a diffusion model into an image generation framework. It enables the generation of natural, realistic preferred images by directly modifying the activation-regularized latent codes without per-image iterative optimization.…

items.title: DynaSolver: A Neural Operator for Autoregressive 4D Flow Prediction with Dynamic Boundaries
items.summary: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD), but most are designed for static geometries and are not equipped to model unsteady flows induced by continuously moving boundaries. We study dynamic-boundary 4D CFD prediction for articulated moving geometries and introduce RoboCFD-4D, a temporally resolved robotic CFD benchmark spanning diverse morphologies and flow conditions. To address the computational and autoregressive challenges of this setting, we propose DynaSolver, a neural operator that explicitly conditions on boundary evolution and causal flow history. DynaSolver employs an efficient physical-token formulation that amortizes point-to-token projection across the operator stack, substantially reducing repeated point-space spatio-temporal computation while retaining accurate point-level reconstruction.…

items.title: Evaluating Uncertainty Calibration in Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) are increasingly used for probabilistic forecasting across diverse domains, yet the reliability of their uncertainty estimates remains poorly understood. In this work, we study uncertainty calibration in probabilistic TSFMs from a broader methodological and empirical perspective. We introduce a taxonomy of how TSFMs represent predictive uncertainty and develop a fine-grained evaluation framework for calibration in multi-horizon forecasting that distinguishes pooled, horizon-wise, and stronger conditional notions of calibration. Using this framework, we conduct a comprehensive empirical evaluation of popular TSFMs across diverse datasets and show that current models exhibit distinct and systematic patterns of miscalibration that standard metrics often obscure.…

items.title: A Scaling Theory of Multi-Epoch Pretraining: Late-Time Overfitting and Ensembling
items.summary: In the near future language model pretraining will become bound by total data rather than total compute. Such a regime requires revisiting scaling laws and scaling law theory. Motivated by prior works that have found utility in ensembling, we study how the number of training epochs and ensemble size jointly shape generalization when training data are fixed. In language-model experiments on FineWeb, logit averaging reduces late-training deterioration, delays optimal stopping, and can outperform wider or deeper single models at matched parameter-token budgets over a common training horizon. To analyze this interaction between data reuse and ensembling, we derive a dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for multi-epoch stochastic gradient descent in power-law random-feature ensembles, tracking error correlations across epochs and models.…

items.title: FedReady: Bounded Agents for Federation Formation
items.summary: Federated learning (FL) runtimes standardize aggregation and deployment, but each new study still requires federation formation: selecting task-eligible sites and preparing their local data and task code for federated training or analysis. This preparation recurs when the target changes, while raw records and site-private mappings are excluded from cross-site FL messages. We present FedReady, a system that performs federation formation with bounded LLM agents. Agents propose shared contracts, local adapters, and task code; the runtime owns workflow state and accepts artifacts only after checks tied to their digests. Candidate site discovery prioritizes recall; local eligibility verification checks task support before site admission. Once participating sites and artifacts are fixed, conventional federated training or analysis proceeds without readiness agents.…

items.title: Sonar-MoE: In-Backward Expert Updates for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training
items.summary: Most parameters of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model belong to its experts, and standard training keeps every expert gradient in GPU memory until the optimizer step. This memory grows with the number and size of the experts, so it rises as MoE models scale. We introduce Sonar-MoE, which updates each expert tensor during the backward pass and frees its gradient right away. It brings optimizer-in-backward from dense models to batched MoE expert tensors, so the GPU never holds more than one layer of expert gradients. When we fine-tune OLMoE-1B-7B and Granite-3.1-3B-A800M in bf16 with two expert-kernel backends, Sonar-MoE lowers peak memory by 19% to 22%. Its updates are bitwise identical to standard training without expert gradient clipping, and held-out loss stays within 0.003 of all baselines. Each step also takes 17% to 23% less time than standard training with global-norm clipping.…

items.title: VeriHarm-Bench: Measuring Harmful Success in LLM Coding Agents Verifiably
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) coding agents increasingly operate with shell access, allowing them to write scripts, move files, alter permissions, and modify system configurations. However, an agent may achieve a user's goal while causing unintended harm, such as deleting unrelated files, weakening access controls, or corrupting data, in response to benign inputs without explicit jailbreaking. This failure mode is particularly important because apparent task success may reassure users that an agent behaved correctly, causing harmful side effects to go unnoticed. We call this harmful success: the agent successfully completes the intended benign task while simultaneously causing unintended harm.…

items.title: PlantVLM-Edge: Quantized Vision-Language Models for On-Device Crop Health Diagnosis
items.summary: Timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is essential for sustainable agricultural production, yet accurate diagnosis often requires expert knowledge that is not readily available. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, and natural-language interaction, creating new opportunities for intelligent crop health assessment. However, deploying VLMs on resource-constrained devices remains challenging due to their substantial computational and memory requirements. This paper presents PlantVLM-Edge, a quantized vision-language framework for conversational crop health diagnosis that can run entirely on resource-constrained edge devices.…

items.title: Variational Functional Neural Networks (vfNN)
items.summary: We present a variational functional neural network (vfNN) algorithm that optimizes physically motivated continuum functionals in integral form (e.g., Lagrangian, Hamiltonian, or free energy) to find the states of a system. That way, vfNN bypasses solving the equations of motion (a.k.a. the Euler-Lagrange equations), which are in the form of differential equations. To this end, our approach is fundamentally different from conventional physics-informed neural networks (PINN) that solve differential equations by minimizing a phenomenological loss function involving higher order derivatives and ad hoc weight factors. In contrast, vfNN merely evaluates lower order derivatives of the generating functional and replaces the weight factors with rigorous physical scales. This also fundamentally changes the loss landscape, and the desired solutions may become unstable.…

items.title: ParaDeAl: Parallel Descent Algorithms for Sparse Statistics
items.summary: Best subset selection is a central problem in statistical regression, drawing increasing attention from the broader optimization and machine learning communities. Solving the hard L0 sparsity constraint directly has been computationally challenging; as a result, most existing work proposes formulations which do not enforce the constraint, but instead use a mix of L0/L1/L2 penalties to encourage sparsity. Modern methods for solving such penalized formulations are tractable for p = 100,000, but give up direct control over sparsity. In this paper, we propose a two-stage proximal gradient descent-based approach which both enforces the sparsity constraint and incorporates L1/L2 penalties, leveraging GPUs for computational acceleration to find approximate solutions.…

items.title: Contrastive Adapter Training and Consensus Knowledge Distillation for Multi-Source-Free Domain Adaptation in Skin Cancer Diagnosis
items.summary: Skin cancer diagnosis, particularly differentiating melanoma from benign nevi, is challenging due to the visual similarity between lesions. Although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs) have shown promising performance, their effectiveness often deteriorates on data from heterogeneous clinical sources. Conventional domain adaptation methods address domain shift but require access to source data during adaptation, which is often infeasible due to privacy regulations. Multi-source-free unsupervised domain adaptation (MSFDA) addresses this limitation by leveraging multiple labeled source domains to generalize to an unlabeled target domain without requiring access to source data.…

items.title: Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime
items.summary: Computer programmers chain together the same reusable computational primitives, for example, conditional statements or loops, but in different orders to implement different algorithms. In contrast, existing language model architectures always execute their layers in the same order. We introduce Library of Layers (LoL), an architecture that dynamically orders its layers during inference to solve the problem at hand. LoL has a single hyperparameter, the size of its global library of transformer blocks, that allows it to transition seamlessly between parameter reuse and sparsity, generalizing the parameter-efficiency and FLOPs-efficiency tradeoffs of dense, depth-recurrent, and mixture of experts architectures in one unified family. We show that LoL achieves competitive performance with all three above baselines when pretrained on text data.…
items.tldr: Library of Layers dynamically orders transformer blocks during inference to adapt computation to tasks, enabling parameter reuse, sparsity, and interpretable routing across reasoning, multilingual, and safety settings.

items.title: DistDebug-Bench: Can LLM Agents Diagnose Bugs in Distributed Systems?
items.summary: LLM agents show strong potential in software engineering tasks such as competitive programming and code synthesis. Existing benchmarks, however, largely focus on small-scale settings such as self-contained Python modules, leaving distributed systems, an essential class of production software, under-examined. We introduce DistDebug-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating agents' ability to diagnose complex-system failures at the code level. It curates 120 high-quality real-world bugs from 11 widely used distributed systems, spanning 5 programming languages and 10 failure patterns. Through an extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs and agents, we identify substantial gaps between current agents and real-world debugging tasks. A recurring gap is tunnel vision due to a lack of explicit reasoning structure and nondeterminism from inconsistent tool-use scope.…

items.title: VIAS: Value-Isolating Activation Steering for Multi-Value Alignment and Compliance for Organisations
items.summary: Organisations increasingly deploy large language model agents that must follow organisational values. We check whether activation steering, which adds vectors to a model's internal activations during generation without changing its weights, can improve compliance beyond prompting alone. Since most scenarios involve several values at once, we focus on multi-value steering. A simple way to build these vectors is to contrast responses that follow all values relevant to a scenario with responses that violate them. However, this gives nearly identical vectors for different values: they capture a general compliance signal rather than individual values, which limits their use when combining several values.…

items.title: RASP: Read-All, Sparse-Plasticity Continual Learning in a Stationary-Size LoRA
items.summary: Parameter-efficient continual learning on pre-trained Vision Transformers largely relies on a costly premise: preventing catastrophic forgetting requires either spawning a dedicated LoRA branch per session---causing adapter parameters to scale linearly with task horizon---or applying sparse Mixture-of-Experts gating symmetrically to both forward and backward passes, which sacrifices representational rank at test time. We argue that reading consolidated knowledge and writing new task credit are fundamentally asymmetric operations. Because visual features in a shared low-rank space distribute across rank-1 atoms rather than localizing in disjoint task silos, forward inference should read all atoms at full rank capacity, whereas backward optimization should restrict plasticity to a sparse subset of input-aligned channels.…

items.title: Axion1-0/axion-training-data
items.summary: Axion 1.0 Training Data Scientific reasoning and tool use for open agent foundation models. Project Page · Paper (Hugging Face) · Paper (PDF) · Code Axion 1.0 follows a three-stage training recipe: learn self-contained reasoning, learn to acquire missing information through tools, then refine these abilities through reinforcement learning.…

items.title: When Robots Outweigh Objects: How Inertia Mismatch Shapes Robot Policy Learning
items.summary: Conventional robot arms can be extremely heavy compared with the everyday objects they manipulate, creating a significant inertia mismatch at contact. Even a small accidental bump from a heavy arm can knock a light object out of place. Modern learning methods have nevertheless demonstrated a wide range of successful manipulation behaviors on these platforms, suggesting that even extreme inertia mismatch can be overcome with sufficient data. However, it remains unclear whether high inertia imposes a hidden cost on learning, potentially worsening scaling with data or lowering the performance ceiling of modern robot learning methods. We investigate this question through controlled simulation experiments that vary robot and object masses.…

items.title: SNAP: Semantic Navigation Among Pedestrians
items.summary: Navigating crowded urban environments requires robots to avoid pedestrians while adhering to social norms such as remaining on sidewalks. Existing approaches typically address either crowd avoidance or semantic path planning in isolation. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) navigation policy that jointly reasons about semantic terrain and dynamic obstacles from a single semantically annotated bird's-eye-view (BEV) map, without relying on explicit human-state estimation. Our policy outperforms established crowd-navigation and semantic-aware baselines and transfers zero-shot to a legged robot, demonstrating socially compliant navigation in highly dynamic real-world scenarios.

items.title: RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills
items.summary: Third-party Agent Skills extend what an autonomous agent can do, but a malicious Skill can hide data exposure or output manipulation inside a legitimate workflow. Neither reading a Skill's description nor granting it tool permissions tells whether its execution meets the user's security requirements. We introduce RuntimeTickets, a protocol that enforces and audits these requirements while a Skill runs. From released malicious-Skill datasets we derive a risk model and build adversarial-benign Skill pairs. From the task's delivery contract, a language model proposes security obligations for that task. Each obligation cites the Skill lines it answers, and the ticket tightens the host's approvals into fine-grained allowed actions but never loosens them.…

items.title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
items.summary: The shear piezoelectric coefficient $e_{15}$ governs the shear-mode electromechanical coupling in piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) and surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, but measuring it typically requires destructive resonance testing on dedicated specimens. On simulated data, $e_{15}$ can instead be recovered non-destructively from sparse, noisy subsurface wavefield observations using a constrained physics-informed neural network (PINN). By building exact spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers directly into the network output, the clamped, grounded boundaries and resting initial state hold automatically, leaving the loss with only the interior equations of coupled electro-elastodynamics and the data misfit.…
