items.title: FACTS-MAS: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Adaptive Forecasting from Heterogeneous Evidence
items.summary: Real-world forecasting often requires integrating heterogeneous evidence whose predictive value varies across horizons, operating regimes, and domains. We introduce FACTS-MAS, a domain-agnostic multi-agent forecasting framework that decomposes evidence into specialized channels for temporal dynamics, exogenous context, seasonality, structural information, and discrete events. Each agent generates an independently testable forecast through a common interface, while leakage-safe historical validation measures its predictive skill relative to a naive reference. These skill estimates are used to weight and combine agent forecasts, so that uninformative evidence is either removed or downweighted rather than forced to participate. A calibration procedure selects domain-specific constant means based on historical validation folds.…

items.title: Silhouette-Based Gaitomics for Frailty Assessment in Older Adults
items.summary: Walking offers a window into physical function that may support interpretable video-based frailty assessment. We developed silhouette-based "gaitomics" to connect frailty predictions with measurable patterns of body configuration and movement. In 66 older adults assessed using the Fried Frailty Phenotype, standardized silhouettes and gait energy images yielded 90 descriptors of shape, temporal variation, motion, and texture. Minimum redundancy maximum relevance selection using the mutual information difference criterion prioritized informative features while limiting redundancy. Each classifier was evaluated using nested stratified cross-validation with five outer and three inner folds at the participant level, with feature ranking and feature-count selection confined to training partitions. Shapley additive explanations examined contributions to held-out predictions.…

items.title: CuraEval: Evaluating Demonstration Curation on Mixed-Skill Robot Data
items.summary: Robot imitation learning uses demonstrations from operators of varying skill, but selecting training data remains challenging. Existing methods score demonstrations using smoothness, diversity, or estimated influence on policy performance, but differences in selection and evaluation protocols make it difficult to determine whether they outperform simple baselines. We introduce \textbf{CuraEval}, a framework combining mathematical analysis of demonstration scores with controlled comparisons against fixed size-matched random subsets and full-data training on mixed-skill robomimic data using Diffusion Policy and BC-RNN. We show that the evaluated PSD score depends only on episode length and squared position magnitudes, and produces nearly the same ranking as episode length on \textit{square} ($ρ=0.999$).…

items.title: Rubricon: Automated Rubric Generation and Refinement for LLM Evaluation and Training
items.summary: Rubrics enable reward assignment on tasks without verifiable answers, but are expensive to manually produce from scratch. We present Rubricon, a pipeline that generates discriminative rubrics without requiring human preference labels, rubric annotation, or generator-model training. Using any LLM, Rubricon samples multiple rubrics, selects the most discriminative candidate, adds criteria to capture overlooked requirements or response flaws, and prunes criteria that are misaligned or shallow. Alongside LLM self-critique and test-time scaling, Rubricon uses observed criterion pass rates on example model responses to guide refinement.…

items.title: HotPOT: Operator Transformer with Heterogeneous Physics Experts for Large-Scale PDE Pre-training
items.summary: Large-scale PDE pre-training trains a single model on the data from multiple partial differential equations (PDEs). However, adding heterogeneous PDEs with different governing equations, physical variables, and variable interactions does not always improve predictive performance across tasks. Existing PDE mixture-of-experts models mitigate cross-task interference through learned routing, but typically use homogeneous expert architectures, making it difficult to directly reflect differences in state evolution across equations. We introduce HotPOT, an operator transformer with heterogeneous physics experts for large-scale PDE pre-training. HotPOT uses a shared encoder to capture information common across PDEs, while each PDE family uses a neural-numerical expert that pairs a learnable predictor with a fixed numerical update containing no trainable parameters.…

items.title: Disparity Laundering: Consensus Without Fairness in Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Clinical large language models are increasingly fielded as multi-agent teams, on the assumption that deliberation averages out individual error. It does not average out bias. Across a full factorial of five model families and four aggregation topologies on 120 real MIMIC-IV emergency cases under counterfactual demographic swaps, no configuration neutralizes the disparity: all 20 cells commit the direction of their agents' independent answers, giving Black patients more acute triage. Every model has a topology that amplifies its baseline gap, but which one varies by model, so no design is reliably safe or reliably amplifying: the disparity is relocated, never removed. Late-stage fixes fail: fairness instructions and demographic masking leave the gap untouched, and per-agent self-debiasing widens it, because the bias is already encoded in the agents' ordinary clinical numbers.…

items.title: Two Birds with One Stone: Skill-Augmented Generation via Unified Retrieval and Utilization
items.summary: Skills, as reusable external knowledge, have demonstrated substantial potential to enhance the ability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to solve complex tasks. However, existing skill-augmented generation methods typically rely on separate models for skill retrieval and skill utilization, resulting in disconnected optimization of these two processes. To address this gap, we propose Skill-Uni, a unified reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes skill retrieval and utilization. Specifically, we adopt a generative skill retrieval paradigm that enables a single model to both learn how to retrieve relevant skills and leverage them for task solving. To effectively train this unified framework, we introduce a two-stage training strategy consisting of warm-up instruction tuning and GRPO, allowing the model to progressively improve its skill retrieval and utilization capabilities.…

items.title: Converting a superseded Raith electron beam pattern generator into an unattended Critical Dimension SEM
items.summary: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. Manual SEM imaging on a wafer-scale is time-intensive, can feature operator-dependent distortions, and yields too few data to reliably close the nanofabrication calibration loop. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction.…

items.title: Embodied at Sea: Imitation Learning for Multi-Task Underwater Manipulation
items.summary: Behavior Cloning has demonstrated promising generalization capabilities for robotic manipulation in terrestrial environments. However, marine visual distortions and dynamic currents create a severe domain shift that remains a key bottleneck in adapting generalist architectures to underwater field manipulation. To address this, 1616 episodes of underwater manipulation data were collected in calm and turbulent waters and were used to train 14 generalist Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models (DynamicVLA) with varying proprioception observation configurations. Across three tasks on 1260 gradable on-hardware rollouts in a pool, 10 models outperformed the baseline, with the highest-performing model achieving a 93.3% overall success rate, including partial successes.…

items.title: Crystoria: A Large-Scale Crystal Dataset Linking Thermodynamic and Dynamical Stability for Materials AI
items.summary: Large-scale crystal databases have transformed materials discovery by making millions of structures and thermodynamic properties accessible to materials informatics. Yet dynamical stability remains sparsely characterized at a comparable scale because its evaluation is substantially more computationally demanding than conventional structure and energy calculations. This mismatch creates a critical gap between the rapidly expanding crystal-structure space and the physical information available for materials research and machine learning. Here we introduce Crystoria, a large-scale crystal dataset designed to bring dynamical stability to the scale of modern materials data.…

items.title: Prototype-Guided Dynamic Domain Modulation and a Large-Scale Multi-SKU Benchmark for Shampoo Bottle Surface Defect Detection
items.summary: Industrial shampoo-bottle surface defect detection must operate across many stock keeping units (SKUs), where differences in bottle geometry, material, label layout, reflectance, and imaging conditions can substantially alter the appearance of the same defect. Existing industrial defect datasets rarely provide both instance-level defect annotations and product-variant identities, making it difficult to study SKU-aware detection under realistic manufacturing conditions. We introduce Bottle-SKU, a large-scale multi-SKU benchmark for shampoo bottle surface defect detection. Bottle-SKU contains 13,119 images, 20,419 instance-level bounding boxes, seven defect categories, and 48 bottle SKUs, enabling evaluation of both shared defect recognition and SKU-specific appearance variation.…

items.title: In-Context Learning for Multi-Fidelity Multiscale Model Closure and Cross-Operator Out-Of-Distribution Generalization
items.summary: Multi-fidelity learning uses low-fidelity information (coarse-scale PDE models) together with limited high-fidelity data (fine-scale solutions) to obtain high-accuracy PDE solutions. It is a data-driven approach to downscale reduced-order models to solve PDEs efficiently and accurately. Standard multi-fidelity learning focuses on one operator or PDE; given a new PDE, retraining using additional coarse-fine solution pairs may be required, which is costly. In this work, we propose an in-context multi-fidelity learning framework for learning multiple multi-fidelity operators with one shared model. The model is trained using paired low- and high-fidelity examples as demonstrations from multiple operators, together with a new coarse-scale solution query, to predict the corresponding fine-scale solution.…

items.title: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms
items.summary: Benders decomposition and column generation solve large optimization problems by passing cuts, columns, and dual values between a master problem and subproblems, and are hard to implement correctly. Large language models now automate parts of algorithm design, which points toward agents that build decomposition solvers for new problems. As a first step toward such agents, we study how well current coding agents design and implement these two algorithms, and how they fail. We introduce DecompGym, 81 instances from nine problem families (five Benders, four column generation), in which an agent writes a solver for a prescribed method. Each solver must meet three criteria: execution within a 60-second time limit; numerical feasibility together with a method audit, in which an LLM judge reads the solver's code; and an objective within 1% of the stored optimal objective.…

items.title: Data Amount Heterogeneity Improves Performance in Federated Learning for Neuroimaging
items.summary: Federated Learning (FL) allows for secure analysis of distributed data without data sharing. We and others have successfully applied FL to neuroimaging tasks, such as Alzheimer's disease classification from structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). FL trains a deep learning model locally at each site, encrypts the local model parameters and sends them to a federation controller that aggregates the local models under homomorphic encryption, the resulting community model is sent back to the sites for further training, and the process repeats for a number of rounds. FL often achieves learning performance (e.g., accuracy) close to centralized training, but no data leaves the sites and model parameters are protected through encryption and other measures.…

items.title: ATI-OPD: Adaptive Teacher Intervention for Stable Long-Sequence On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own responses using token-level feedback from a teacher. As responses grow longer, the student's prefix can depart from the teacher's own reasoning, weakening its feedback on later tokens. Updates based on this feedback can reinforce the same deviations in later responses and destabilize training. Prior approaches such as length control and loss reweighting limit learning from problematic responses but leave their prefixes unchanged. Fixed cutoffs can also discard later reasoning. We propose \textbf{Adaptive Teacher Intervention for On-Policy Distillation (ATI-OPD)} to improve subsequent teacher guidance by revising the student's reasoning prefix. ATI-OPD replaces the earliest high-disagreement segment with a short teacher segment, then lets the student resume its own reasoning from the revised text.…

items.title: MASS: Multi-mask Selective Self-Distillation for Leakage-Resilient Reasoning
items.summary: On-policy self-distillation enables the same model to act as student and teacher, with dense token-level supervision obtained by the teacher being given access to privileged information. However, conditioning the teacher on a single reference can concentrate its predictions on one reasoning trajectory and limit transfer to the student. We propose Multi-Mask Selective Self-Distillation (MASS), which approximates the unavailable marginal over diverse reference realizations using multiple independently masked views of one verified solution. MASS aggregates these complementary teacher predictions, selectively transfers reliable token-level corrections, and adaptively focuses masking on influential reference spans. Across mathematical reasoning benchmarks and model families, MASS consistently outperforms strong self-distillation baselines.

items.title: BridgeRouter: Gain-Aware Instance Routing over Cross-Modal Bridge Portfolios
items.summary: Lightweight representation bridges make pretrained, task-adapted EEG foundation models executable on other biosignal modalities without retraining their backbones. However, selecting a single bridge pathway globally assigns every instance to the same transfer route and ignores complementary errors across routes. We therefore formulate multi-bridge transfer as an instance-level algorithm-selection problem and introduce BridgeRouter, a gain-aware router over a portfolio of frozen cross-modal pathways. A validation-selected Single Best Solver (SBS) serves as a protected default route. During training, task labels are used to compute the reduction in negative log-likelihood provided by each alternative route relative to the SBS, and a lightweight MLP predicts these route-specific gains from a target-modality representation extracted by a frozen encoder.…

items.title: Decompose, Don't Expand: Capability-Independent AI Systems by Construction
items.summary: A recurring design choice in building AI systems is whether, when a task is too hard for a model, to expand the model (make it larger, better-prompted, fine-tuned), or to decompose the task (extract the parts that admit a deterministic solution to a host, leaving the model only the irreducibly fuzzy residue). We make three claims. First, that many tasks commonly delegated whole to a model are in fact deterministic tasks with a small generative core. Second, and our central empirical result, that decomposing such a task yields a measurable and desirable property we call parity by construction: on the extracted sub-tasks the model-size performance curve becomes flat, because no model performs them at all.…

items.title: aa1143/NamiGPT
items.summary: 零基础入门大模型（LLM）的基础教程：从零手写 GPT-2，一行行看懂大模型是怎么工作的 | Build GPT-2 from scratch in PyTorch, step by step

items.title: Post-Training Large Language Models with LLMON
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) treat all context tokens uniformly, lacking explicit separation between executable instructions and passive data. This leads to prompt injection vulnerabilities, ambiguous instruction binding, and unreliable execution control. We present a post-training methodology using LLMON (LLM Object Notation), a framework that enables separating instructions from data and requires explicit identifier-based execution. We construct a large-scale structured training corpus of 4.6B tokens spanning general, RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), and tool-calling data, augmented with distractor-infused variants in which competing instructions and irrelevant data segments are present in context but not referenced.…

items.title: FPGAFly: A 166.7k-Neuron Fruit-Fly Connectome on One FPGA via Deferred Spike Expansion and Shared-Codeword States
items.summary: Synapse-resolution fruit-fly (Drosophila) connectomes enable neuron-by-neuron simulation of entire insect nervous systems, yet whole-brain models still require computationally demanding software or multiple neuromorphic chips, and single FPGAs support only small or statistical networks. Scaling to the full connectome, per-synapse spike expansion scales queue traffic with fan-out up to 11.2k, while 41-bit neuron states require 6.83 Mbit, exceeding the 6.27 Mbit on-chip block static RAM (BSRAM) of the target device. FPGAFly runs the 166.7k-neuron, 25.6M-connection leaky integrate-and-fire male central nervous system (CNS) connectome on one FPGA. Order-preserving deferred expansion queues one 64-bit descriptor per spike in source-ID order, cutting external memory traffic by 54.5%-57.9% and peak queue data by 95.6%-96.5% with bit-identical results.…

items.title: Experimental Demonstration of Double-Fourier Interferometer Imaging for Future Space-Based Far-Infrared Observatories
items.summary: Far-infrared (FIR) astronomy is crucial for observing star formation, active galactic nuclei, and protoplanetary systems, but its effectiveness is severely limited by poor diffraction-limited spatial resolution. To overcome this limitation, a double-Fourier interferometer (DFI), which couples a spatial interferometer with a Fourier transform spectrometer, has been proposed to deliver high-resolution broadband spectral imaging. Despite various conceptual and prototype studies, a comprehensive demonstration of DFI capabilities has been lacking. In this study, we present the validation of key DFI observing techniques using a laboratory testbed operating in the 0.3 to 2.1 THz optical bandwidth. We detail the instrument's ideal response alongside necessary calibrations for intensity imbalances, non-linear phase errors, and phase-center offsets.…

items.title: Same Label, Different Interface: Beyond Action-Space Labels in Robot Learning
items.summary: Robot-learning studies often compare position and velocity actions as though each label identified a single experimental treatment, yet the label alone does not determine what the robot executes. Before affecting robot motion, bounded policy output passes through filtering, physical scaling, reference construction, feedback, timing, and effort limits. We study how these omitted properties affect attribution under one shared learner and training budget. Across three contact-rich Factory tasks (PegInsert, GearMesh, and NutThread), we compare five joint-space interfaces, with ten independently trained policies per condition.…

items.title: Evaluating Causal Reasoning in LLMs: A Case Study in the Challenges of Procedural Generation
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) appear to represent and reason about a large range of phenomena. In particular, recent studies have examined whether LLMs can accurately reason about causation. One of the most commonly used benchmarks for evaluating formal causal reasoning in LLMs is CLadder, a framework for procedural generation of benchmark data sets that was released in 2023. Experiments with CLadder appear to indicate that LLMs can perform formal causal reasoning in a large percentage of generated examples. In this paper, we examine what can be reliably inferred when LLMs perform well on test sets produced by CLadder. We identify several examples of superficial and highly predictive patterns that the CLadder generator embeds in data sets it generates.…

items.title: Jailbreak Connectivity: Towards Diverse, Transferable, and Universal Multimodal Large Language Model Jailbreak
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are vulnerable to visual jailbreak attacks that bypass safety safeguards. Existing methods typically optimize isolated adversarial examples, limiting attack diversity, transferability, and generalization. We propose Jailbreak Connectivity (JC), a framework based on the observation that effective adversarial inputs can be connected through low-loss regions in image space. JC optimizes continuous adversarial paths: path sampling yields diverse jailbreak images, lightweight surrogate classifiers guide cross-model transfer, and a distribution-level objective enables universal attacks across harmful queries. On MM-SafetyBench, JC achieves average attack success rates of 84.01%, 85.77%, and 97.95% on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, InternVL3.5-8B, and Gemma-3-12B-IT, respectively, exceeding the strongest baselines by up to 68.36 percentage points.…

items.title: Multi-Token Prediction Done Right
items.summary: Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) is now a common ingredient in language-model pre-training, as it improves downstream performance and enables faster inference through speculative decoding. We identify a flaw in standard MTP training, in which a residual component of the MTP gradient interferes with both next-token and multi-token learning, increasingly so with scale. Specifically, the MTP cross-entropy gradient can be decomposed exactly into a KL self-distillation term that pulls each MTP head toward the model's own next-token prediction (NTP) distribution and improves speculative decoding, and a residual that has a low signal-to-noise ratio and buries the useful KL signal.…
items.tldr: Soft-MTP removes a noisy gradient residual from multi-token prediction via a straight-through KL recovery trick, improving perplexity, speculative decoding, and reasoning without added cost.

items.title: Scaling Lean Theorem Proving for Real-World Code Verification
items.summary: We present EasyProver, a Lean proving system built from recursive agents with isolated contexts, asynchronous search, parallel tactic probing, and an elastic elaboration service. Using an off-the-shelf frontier model with no additional training, it proves 669/672 PutnamBench problems and all six IMO 2026 formalizations and resolves 597/600 NTP4VC verification conditions and all 189 VERINA tasks by proof or refutation. Because these benchmarks are close to saturation, we also introduce Aegis, which converts competitive programming problems into much harder verification tasks over real implementations. The pipeline writes safe Rust solutions, translates them into Lean with Aeneas, generates specifications, and labels each frozen statement with a kernel-checked proof or refutation. It produces 2,045 differentially validated Rust-Lean program pairs and 11,533 candidate specifications.…
items.tldr: EasyProver is a Lean proving system using recursive agents and asynchronous search that solves nearly all Putnam and IMO benchmark problems, while Aegis generates harder verification tasks from competitive programming to benchmark provers and support reinforcement learning.

items.title: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video
items.summary: Producing long-form videos from narration requires interdependent decisions that remain coherent across shots. Existing agentic editors often use multi-stage workflows driven by general models, leaving the quality-cost trade-off of compact, task-adapted policies unclear. We address this gap with WeVisCut, a long-form script-to-video system that connects tool execution with policy learning. Its agent harness maintains shared production state so that tool feedback informs subsequent decisions and repairs. Because finished videos do not expose these decisions, our four-stage data pipeline combines editing inversion with verified replay to turn recovered editing intent into executable supervision. Applied to 3,750 finished videos, this pipeline yields over 130K training examples.…
items.tldr: WeVisCut is a script-to-video system that trains a compact policy to coordinate video editing tools, recover from failures, and reduce token usage while maintaining quality.

items.title: Investor's Last Exam: Can AI Agents Do Equity Investment Without Seeing the Future?
items.summary: Financial agents must form forecasts and investment judgments from decision-time evidence, with predictions evaluated against subsequent outcomes. Existing benchmarks assess financial knowledge, research workflows, or forecasting, but evaluating the full research process requires a strictly frozen information set and professional evaluation criteria. We introduce Investor's Last Exam (ILE), an equity-research benchmark led by experienced buy-side investors and fund managers. Its three components are a versioned financial database spanning 3.43 million document versions and nine source categories, supplemented by structured market data, with validated timestamps governing retrieval and computation; a task taxonomy organized around professional analyst deliverables; and an expert-led framework linking scoring criteria to sources, calculations, and assumptions through financial dependency…
items.tldr: Investor's Last Exam evaluates financial agents on end-to-end equity research using frozen evidence, expert criteria, and dependency graphs, revealing that top models excel at research but fail at forecasting and investment judgments.

items.title: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement requires models not only to acquire useful training experience, but also to decide when their current experience has ceased to be useful. Existing methods often focus on what experience to generate next, while paying less attention to when fresh experience should be introduced. Many also construct training targets through self-consistency or majority voting, making supervision depend on the model's own uncertain predictions. We address these two questions separately: training dynamics determine when to acquire new experience, while the answers to new tasks remain independently checkable. A-RSI monitors reward variation and accuracy in training logs to refresh a task pool when its learning signal declines, without consulting validation or test scores.…
items.tldr: A-RSI improves recursive self-improvement by refreshing training tasks based on declining learning signals and using independently verifiable program-generated answers, raising benchmark performance without external labels.

items.title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation
items.summary: Humans routinely consume multimodal content, where textual and visual information is naturally interleaved. Although Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) can jointly generate text and images, multimodal interleaved generation remains largely underexplored. Progress in this area is hindered by two key limitations: (1) the lack of well-defined interleaved generation tasks and corresponding training data, and (2) the absence of fine-grained evaluation protocols that can reliably diagnose model performance across different capability dimensions. To this end, we present IntReal, comprising two complementary components: IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset of multimodal interleaved samples spanning four major categories, and the IntReal Evaluation Suite, which evaluates model performance across seven complementary dimensions using specialized expert models, enabling coarse-to-fine diagnosis.…
items.tldr: IntReal introduces a real-world interleaved multimodal dataset and evaluation framework to diagnose unified model strengths and improve generation through targeted training.

items.title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding
items.summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models have increased interest in interaction paradigms for video understanding. The evolution from offline to streaming and proactive interaction has gradually shifted models from passive responders toward more proactive agents that can decide when to answer. However, existing proactive paradigms typically assume that the information required to answer a query is complete, leaving models to only wait or answer. In the real world, however, information is often incomplete due to uncertainty from either the video or the user. In proactive paradigms, such uncertainty can cause the model to wait forever or generate highly hallucinatory responses. We therefore argue that proactive interaction should be redefined with a third action: ask, allowing models to actively ask for missing information.…
items.tldr: Proactive video understanding should include asking for missing information under uncertainty, and the AskStream benchmark reveals current models struggle with this decision.

items.title: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
items.summary: Self-distillation offers a way to improve reasoning models when a suitable external teacher is unavailable. However, common approaches rely on privileged information to construct a stronger self-teacher, limiting their use when only unlabeled prompts are available. In this paper, we introduce Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation (WISD), which instead constructs a weaker counterpart of the original model and uses the contrast between the two as a training signal without requiring privileged information. We explore two ways to construct the weaker model: low-bit quantization and magnitude pruning. We evaluate WISD across diverse architectures and scales on mathematical and coding reasoning tasks.…
items.tldr: WISD improves reasoning models by contrasting them with weaker quantized or pruned versions to generate training signals without privileged data.

items.title: Delusions Emerge and Persist due to Generative Model Reorganisation: Insights from Hybrid Predictive Coding
items.summary: Predictive coding has influenced many conceptual accounts of delusions, the impervious and often bizarre beliefs that accompany a range of neuropsychiatric conditions. However, these explanations remain incomplete and have rarely been tested using formal modelling. Here, we present a formal account of delusional beliefs based on hybrid predictive coding, which sheds new light on the computational mechanisms underpinning two core features of delusions: their thematic recurrence and imperviousness to contradictory evidence. In simulation experiments, we demonstrate that a combination of contextually inadequate initialisation of beliefs and excessive certainty in them (a hallmark of psychosis) triggers a reorganisation of the generative model relating observed events to hidden causes.…

items.title: Domain Adaptation Improves Cross-site Classification of First-episode Schizophrenia from Multimodal Neuroimaging Data
items.summary: Identifying robust neuroimaging markers associated with schizophrenia is essential for advancing research and informing clinical understanding. However, a major obstacle to clinical translation is the limited ability of neuroimaging-based classification models to generalize across scanning sites. In this study, we first establish best performing within-site models, and then systematically investigate cross-site generalization in first-episode schizophrenia (FES) classification and evaluate strategies for mitigating site-related distribution shifts. Using data from two acquisition sites (n=544), we examine ComBat, CovBat, optimal transport, and deep adaptation.…

items.title: Flexible compression of sensory evidence makes human decisions more resilient to noisy neural computations
items.summary: Categorizing ambiguous stimuli requires accumulating sensory evidence over time through noisy neural computations. Theories disagree on whether this evidence is accumulated in its native sensory space or in an abstract and compressed category space that retains only decision-relevant information. Here we designed a visual categorization task in which revealing decision categories before or after a stimulus sequence determines which space can be used to accumulate evidence, without changing the optimal decision. Humans were more accurate, and their inferences less noisy, when they could accumulate evidence in category space. Concurrent magnetoencephalographic (MEG) recordings revealed flexible and accuracy-predictive representations of evidence compressed onto decision categories in these conditions.…

items.title: Modelling Audio-Visual Reaction Time with Recurrent Mean-Field Networks
items.summary: Audio-visual stimuli are typically detected faster and more accurately than unisensory ones, but it remains unclear whether this benefit reflects true integration of evidence or other effects such as independent processing and modality repetition. We address this with three biologically motivated models of audio-visual integration, built on Wong and Wang model, a mean-field recurrent framework originally developed for unisensory decision-making. The OR model takes in independent unisensory processes through winner-take-all competition, and the SUM model implements full linear summation of sensory evidence. These two sit at opposite ends of the integration spectrum. The REPEAT model adds switch and repeat costs, whereby responses are faster when the modality repeats across trials.…

items.title: Individual differences in artificial neural networks capture individual differences in human behavior
items.summary: Human behavior differs substantially across individuals. While artificial neural networks (ANNs) are regarded as promising models of human perception, they are often assumed to lack such individual differences. Here, we demonstrate that multiple instances of the same ANN architecture exhibit substantial individual differences in behavior that mimic those observed in humans. We trained and tested 60 ANN instances from three architectures on a digit recognition task and found notable individual differences in overall accuracy, confidence, and response time (RT). Critically, these individual differences in ANN instances mapped consistently onto the individual differences produced by 60 humans performing the same task, with the mapping strength often approaching the human-to-human benchmark across all three behavioral metrics (accuracy, confidence, RT).…

items.title: Linking microscopic and mean-field descriptions ofdopaminergic modulation in neural circuits
items.summary: Next-generation neural mass models capture the collective behavior of brain regions through an exact mean-field reduction of the spiking neural networks, retaining key microscopic properties while remaining computationally efficient. This explicit link to single-neuron dynamics makes them a natural framework for studying how neuromodulators, such as dopamine (DA), shape macroscopic network activity. Integrating its effect is a key step toward biologically grounded brain models. Because the spiking network underlying such a reduction is fully known, the reduced model can be directly validated against it.…

items.title: PHACTn enables training-free, context-independent inference of nucleotide variant tolerance across the genome
items.summary: Accurate prediction of single-nucleotide variant (SNV) tolerability across the entire human genome remains a fundamental challenge in computational genomics, particularly for non-coding regions where the regulatory landscape is vast and poorly understood. Machine learning classifiers suffer from data circularity and demographic bias, while genomic language models demand massive computational resources and offer little biological interpretability. Here, we present PHACTn (Phylogeny-Aware Computing of Tolerance for nucleotide variants), a training-free, parameter-minimal method that infers nucleotide variant tolerability by traversing the mammalian phylogenetic tree and explicitly modeling the evolutionary independence of observed substitutions and their distance from the query species.…

items.title: Verifiable Agentic Science on Public Infrastructure
items.summary: Autonomous artificial intelligence agents are transforming the practice of science. Across every discipline, researchers are handing data analysis to coding agents that can design and execute complex studies from a single prompt. Yet this revolution carries a threat. When agents improvise in local environments, they leave no verifiable record, ultimately risking a wave of irreproducible science. Solving this crisis requires moving agentic science onto public infrastructure where every action leaves an examinable trail. Here we connect autonomous coding agents to shared computing resources, turning ephemeral prompts into auditable scientific records.…

items.title: PepPr: De Novo peptide sequencing with peptide priors
items.summary: Mass spectrometry-based peptide sequencing underpins proteomics. Database search confines to predefined candidates, whereas de novo peptide sequencing (DNPS) struggles with incomplete spectra. Existing hybrid methods use databases only for post hoc correction or retrieve previously identified spectra to guide decoding. We instead combine DNPS with a peptide prior: a language model fitted to a reference proteome, tolerating variants yet uncertain on strongly divergent sequences. Relative to prior-free DNPS, our implementation, PepPr, improved reference peptide identification and improved rather than suppressed variant identification. Using a related proteome as prior, it matched or outperformed homology-driven database search, and its gain over prior-free DNPS grew with relatedness.…

items.title: Neopep: Reinforcement Learning From Machine-Learned Force Field Energy for Non-Canonical Peptide Structure Prediction
items.summary: Peptide therapeutics occupy a compelling middle ground between small molecules and larger proteins, and in practice, most approved peptide drugs incorporate non-canonical amino acids (ncAAs) or other non-peptidic chemistries to elicit improved physiochemical properties (Yaseen Khan et al. (2026)). The chemical space of known ncAAs numbers in the thousands, yet current state-of-theart sequence-to-structure prediction models handle them poorly, because fewer than 0.02% of residues deposited in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) (Berman et al. (2003)), the main source of training data, correspond to ncAAs. Our central idea is that this data bottleneck can be overcome by coupling generative structure prediction with reinforcement learning (RL) from machine-learned force field (MLFF)-derived energy.…

items.title: Multiplex-GCN Predicts Clinically Actionable Tumor Microenvironment Subtypes in Pancreatic Cancer
items.summary: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most lethal cancers worldwide. It has a five-year survival rate of approximately 13%, largely due to late diagnosis, rapid metastasis, and limited therapeutic options. The tumor microenvironment (TME), including immune and non-immune cells, plays a role in PDAC progression and drug resistance. However, molecular characteristics of PDAC based on TME-based subtypes are not well studied. To address this, we developed a multi-layered Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) to identify TME-guided PDAC subtypes. First, we constructed a TME reference atlas using single-cell RNA-seq data comprising immune and non-immune cell types. Second, we applied in silico cytometry to estimate cell-type proportions in bulk tumor RNA-seq samples from the Cancer Genome Atlas PDAC patients.…

items.title: Binning-based Methods for Model Fitting and Data Splitting Improve Machine Learning Imbalanced Regression
items.summary: Modelling quantitative genomics data remains challenging due to imbalanced target distributions, non-independent observations, and substantial computational costs. This study examines the challenges and current methods, proposes new methods, applies these methods across two case studies: a controlled setting with synthetically generated data and on real genomics datasets. Effective modelling of imbalanced data starts with density estimation. Density estimation via binning facilitates downstream analytical steps. Minimum Transformation Binning is a novel method that improves current binning methods for density estimation. Data splitting of imbalanced and non-independent observations is best accomplished by objective data splitting which entails randomly generating splits, scoring them, and selecting the best scoring one.…

items.title: Beyond profiles: supervised repeat annotation using protein embeddings
items.summary: Protein repeats give rise to diverse protein structures and functions, yet their sequence-based detection is often challenging because individual repeat units can diverge substantially in sequence while retaining similar structures. Most sensitive approaches rely on sequence information directly represented by alignments or derived profiles, thereby limiting flexibility and scalability. Here, we introduce TREAD (Transfer learning-based REpeat Annotation using Protein EmbeDdings), a supervised framework that reformulates repeat detection as a residue-level annotation problem and operates directly on embeddings from protein language models. Instead of constructing explicit probabilistic profiles, TREAD learns repeat-specific features implicitly, enabling residue-resolved scoring and flexible repeat segment extraction.…

items.title: Data coherence over data volume drives generalisable genome-based prediction of microbial carbon utilisation
items.summary: Microbial carbon utilisation shapes ecological niches, community assembly, and nutrient cycling, yet remains difficult to predict from genomes despite well-characterised pathways. Genome-based machine-learning models often generalise poorly across datasets, a limitation commonly attributed to small or taxonomically biased training sets. We integrated binary growth phenotypes for 819 strains across 240 carbon sources from four datasets, focusing on 15 shared sources. Cross-dataset evaluation reduced balanced accuracy from 0.86 (within datasets) to 0.62, and restricting evaluation to in-clade relatives recovered only 0.03 of this loss. Because phylogeny alone could not explain the transfer gap, we restricted training to samples with coherent genotype-phenotype relationships, defined by agreement between experimental labels and annotated pathways.…

items.title: Oyster: A Neural Network for Modeling Genomic Sequences with Exact Position-Specific k-mer Contributions
items.summary: Genomics data are sequences, and exploration in these data involves mapping these sequences to function and understanding that mapping. Analogous to a sentence composed of words, a sequence's function is understood through its constituent subsequences, or k-mers. The presence of k-mers, their positions, and their relationships with other k-mers (k-mer associations) all affect sequence function. Understanding the sequence function requires determining the contributions of each of its k-mers and the impacts of their positions and k-mer associations. k-mer associations are inherently combinatorial and may be hierarchical. Although these associations may be impactful for biological phenomena, k-mer associations cannot be understood by humans and severely obfuscate model analyses, yielding generalizations, simplifications, and approximations.…

items.title: Multi-resolution humanness scoring of antibodies via a region-isolated language model
items.summary: Antibodies recognized as foreign can elicit anti-drug antibodies that compromise efficacy and safety, making humanness scoring, estimating how human-like a sequence appears, an early, repeated step in antibody development. Widely used scores reduce a variable domain to a single framework-dominated number, leaving the complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) grafted during humanization, diversified by generative models weakly supervised and rarely audited. Here we introduce IgScope, a 23-million-parameter antibody language model trained from scratch that scores humanness at chain, IMGT-region, and residue resolution; a region-isolated attention module confines attention to within-region pairs, and chimeric-sequence training supplies region-level supervision.…

items.title: High-throughput mapping of kinase-substrate interactions with protein language models and phospho-PCA
items.summary: Protein phosphorylation is a key regulator of cellular physiology, yet major gaps remain in our understanding of the human kinome. A substantial fraction of measured human phosphosites lacks an assigned upstream kinase, and roughly a third of the human kinome remains functionally undercharacterized. This disconnect limits our ability to understand how the rewiring of cell signaling contributes to disease. In this work, we bridge this gap by developing a lab-in-the-loop framework for understanding and predicting kinase-substrate interactions (KSIs). We combine KINBERT, a protein language model that jointly encodes catalytic domains and substrate peptides to learn interaction rules, with the phosphorylation protein complementation assay (phospho-PCA), a screening platform that enables the simultaneous, pooled profiling of thousands of substrates against multiple kinases.…

items.title: Creator 1.0: Phylogeny-Guided Stagewise Pretraining for Plant Genome Foundation Models across 1,000 Species
items.summary: Genomic language models have advanced DNA sequence analysis, but their applicability to plant-specific tasks and representation changes during pretraining remain poorly characterized. Here, we present Creator 1.0, a 2-billion-parameter parameter plant genome foundation model pretrained on 1,000 plant genomes using phylogeny-guided stagewise pretraining (PGSP). Training comprised 83 consecutive stages and produced 52 cumulative checkpoints associated with distinct plant orders. On GENEB, the stage 83 checkpoint ranked first among 46 models across 10 plant-related tasks, with a mean Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.565, and fourth across all 100 tasks. Evaluation of 52 checkpoints on six plant lncRNA tasks identified different optimal stages under full-data, 10-shot and 1-shot settings, corresponding to stages 71, 72 and 29, respectively.…

items.title: Spatial AI quantification of inflammatory and architectural features differentiates pathologist-defined active ulcerative colitis from histological remission
items.summary: Background and AimsArtificial intelligence (AI) is applied to histological assessment in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), but most approaches quantify features without considering anatomical location. We developed and evaluated PAIR-IBD (Perspectum AI Reading in IBD), an AI system quantifying inflammatory cell, crypt injury, and epithelial damage within mucosal compartments to distinguish histologically-defined active disease, remission, and inconclusive cases in ulcerative colitis (UC), in a single clinical network. MethodsA deep-learning ensemble was trained on three IBD datasets to identify lymphocytes, neutrophils, eosinophils, and plasma cells, and segment crypts, lamina propria (LP), surface epithelium and muscularis mucosae. Inflammatory cell densities and crypt injury metrics (mucin depletion, solidity, roughness, branching, and abscesses) were quantified.…

items.title: Corticospinal and Reticulospinal-Associated Measures in Chronic Ischemic Stroke: Associations with Upper Limb Function
items.summary: BackgroundCorticospinal tract (CST) damage is the main cause of post-stroke motor impairment. Whilst the output of the reticulospinal tract (RST) is reportedly upregulated, its relation to CST damage post-stroke is unclear. We assessed CST integrity using transcranial magnetic stimulation and RST activity using the StartReact paradigm in chronic ischemic stroke and examined their inter-relationship and associations with upper-limb impairment. MethodsWe included 80 patients with chronic ischemic stroke and 15 age-matched healthy controls (HCs). CST function was quantified using the resting motor threshold asymmetry index (RMT-AI); RST function was measured by the StartReact effect (visual-auditory minus visual-startle reaction time) during isometric wrist flexion.…

items.title: NOVA Through Two Lenses: From Nutrients to Food Processing Classification in Finland's National Food Database
items.summary: Ultra-processed food (UPF) intake has been linked to adverse health outcomes. However, NOVA processing groups are hard to assign consistently, and many national food composition databases do not include them. Nutrient-based classification models could fill this gap, but their performance across countries and databases is uncertain. FoodProX is a machine-learning classifier that predicts NOVA groups and a continuous food-processing score (FPro) from nutrient composition. To test whether such models transfer across databases, we retrained it on 182,344 mostly European Open Food Facts products. We evaluated it on 45,526 held-out Open Food Facts products and, without retraining, on 2,971 NOVA-labelled foods from a US database (FNDDS). We then applied it to the Finnish national food composition database (Fineli), which has no NOVA labels.…

items.title: Quantifying Localized Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes by Deep Learning on H&E Images: Analytical Validation and Prognostic Value in Lung Adenocarcinoma
items.summary: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are a critical determinant of response to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). However, assessing the clinical utility of TIL quantification is challenging due to subjective manual scoring and differences in methodology, including some that may obscure localized immune responses critical to ICI response. Together, these issues limit our understanding of potential prognostic benefits of performing routine TIL quantification. Here, we present the "focal TIL score," an artificial intelligence-powered biomarker derived from routinely generated Hematoxylin & Eosin (H&E) pathology images which measures TIL density within tiles across the entire relevant tissue region in order to account for spatial heterogeneity of localized lymphocytic infiltration.…

items.title: Evaluating ChatGPTs Responses to Chiropractic Patient Questions: A Comparative Study
items.summary: BackgroundLarge language models (LLMs) are used at an increased frequency by patients to answer health related questions. Prior studies have evaluated LLMs and their performance with musculoskeletal (MSK) and spine domains, but have not been used to evaluate chiropractic-relevant content. ObjectiveTo evaluate ChatGPT responses to commonly asked chiropractic patient questions for concordance with chiropractic clinical practice guidelines. MethodsThirty questions addressing low back pain, neck pain, and chronic musculoskeletal pain were developed based on current U.S. chiropractic clinical practice guidelines (CPGs). ChatGPT (GPT-5.2) generated responses in isolated sessions.…

items.title: Large language models detect methodological errors that human peer review misses in clinical trials
items.summary: BackgroundPeer review is the principal quality control of published research, but methodological errors can go undetected. In an earlier experiment with errors inserted into three reports of randomized clinical trials, untrained human reviewers achieved a mean major-error detection score of 27%. MethodsWe tested whether 15 large language models (LLMs), including four open-weight models, detect the same errors. To reduce the risk of memorization, we repeated the test on 58 randomized clinical trials published in 2026, including all eligible phase 3 trials. In total, 1,796 reviews were scored by two blinded LLM judges. ResultsOn the original reports, the models major-error detection scores ranged from 53% to 96%. On the 2026 trials, scores ranged from 58% to 99%, and from 66% to 89% for the open-weight models.…

items.title: Richer database context improves LLM-generated EHR phenotyping algorithms
items.summary: ObjectiveTo evaluate large language model (LLM) generation of type 2 diabetes (T2DM) phenotyping SQL and the effect of database implementation context. Materials and MethodsEight publicly accessible LLM-based systems generated SQL under progressively richer prompts using synthetic and University of North Carolina (UNC) Health electronic health record (EHR) data, both based on the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) model. Outputs were compared with the Electronic Medical Records and Genomics (eMERGE) T2DM reference phenotype using SQL executability, F1, positive predictive value (PPV), and recall. ResultsFewer than 55% of limited-context synthetic outputs and no limited-context UNC EHR outputs executed without modification.…

items.title: Actinic keratosis labeling and single-band instability in near-infrared spectroscopy of skin cancer: a nested, patient-level re-analysis
items.summary: BackgroundPortable near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy has been proposed as an adjunct for skin-lesion triage, and the public NIR-SC-UFES dataset has made in vivo NIR spectra of skin lesions available for machine-learning benchmarks. Two questions that bear on how such benchmarks should be read have received little attention: how results depend on the labeling of actinic keratosis (ACK), a pre-malignant lesion that the dataset convention places in the non-cancer group, and whether the wavelengths that classifiers rank as important are stable enough to support spectroscopic interpretation. MethodsWe analyzed the original NIR-SC-UFES file (714 in vivo spectra, 331 patients, 908-1676 nm, 125 points; MicroNIR Pro 1700).…

items.title: Post-implantation 3-T MRI in patients with an epicranial stimulation device: image quality and deep learning-based electrode reconstruction
items.summary: We evaluated structural and functional MRI at 3 T in five patients with an implanted EASEE focal cortex stimulation system and assessed MRI-only electrode reconstruction. Image quality was evaluated visually and by comparing implant-centered and control regions using structural GM/WM signal ratios, GE-EPI signal intensity, T2*, and relative off-resonance. A deep learning pipeline trained exclusively on synthetic data estimated electrode position from T1-weighted MPRAGE images. Structural and functional acquisitions were completed in all patients without scan-related adverse events. Structural images showed clear intracranial anatomy beneath the implant without visually apparent local signal loss or distortion. GE-EPI reference images and derived maps showed no consistent local disturbance corresponding to the electrode.…

items.title: Biopsy-Validated Deep Learning Mapping of Glioma Infiltration Beyond Contrast Enhancement Using Multiparametric MRI
items.summary: BackgroundGlioblastoma (GBM) exhibits diffuse tumor infiltration beyond contrast-enhancing margins into FLAIR-hyperintense brain tissue, where infiltrative tumor is not visible on conventional MRI. We developed and validated the infiltrative Tumor Burden (iTB) map, a deep learning biomarker that uses multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) to identify infiltrative tumor within these non-enhancing regions. MethodsPreoperative mpMRI datasets from 80 patients with WHO grade II-IV gliomas and 24 patients with brain metastases were retrospectively analyzed. Imaging included pre- and post-contrast T1-weighted, T2-weighted, FLAIR, dynamic susceptibility contrast perfusion and diffusion MRI-derived maps (rCBV, rCBF, ADC).…

items.title: Deep Learning-Based Spatial Profiling Identifies MET-Associated Immune Exclusion and Therapeutic Vulnerability Underlying Racial Disparities in Head and Neck Cancer
items.summary: Black/African American (BAA) patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) experience more aggressive disease and poorer survival outcomes than White patients; however, the tumor immune microenvironmental features underlying these racial disparities remain poorly characterized. Here, we identify MET as a potential molecular link between immune exclusion and therapeutic response associated with racial disparities in HNSCC. Compared with White-derived tumors, deep learning-based spatial profiling revealed a distinct immune landscape in BAA-derived tumors, characterized by reduced CD8 T cell infiltration, increased immune checkpoint expression, and elevated spatial MET expression.…

items.title: EM-BENCH: A Reproducible Framework for Benchmarking Guideline-Concordant Clinical Decision Making in Large Language Models
items.summary: BackgroundPhysicians increasingly use artificial intelligence tools to support clinical work, yet there is no accepted standard for measuring the competency of large language models (LLMs) in clinical decision support. We developed EM-BENCH, a physician-validated, deterministically scored benchmark for evaluating whether models reliably apply the American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) guidelines to clinical decisions. MethodsEM-BENCH comprises 210 binary clinical vignettes covering all 70 critical questions across 25 ACEP clinical policies. We evaluated 149 LLM configurations representing 79 base models using prespecified answers and deterministic scoring. Each vignette had a prespecified correct answer to a binary yes-or-no question based on an ACEP recommendation. We examined associations between accuracy and model access tier (closed-access vs.…

items.title: Diurnal Glycemic Redistribution in Obesity Despite Matched Mean Glucose
items.summary: Background and AimsMean glucose and HbA1c reflect average glycemic exposure but do not capture its 24-hour distribution. When average glycemia is comparable, whether obesity is associated with a distinct temporal glucose pattern remains unclear. We compared continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) profiles in lean adults and adults with obesity matched for mean glucose. MethodsIn a cross-sectional AI-READI analysis, lean adults (BMI 18.5-<25 kg/m{superscript 2}) were matched one-to-one to adults with obesity (BMI [≥]30 kg/m{superscript 2}) by recruitment center and clinical group, with calipers for age, mean glucose and glucose standard deviation. CGM profiles were compared by clock time and relative to wearable-defined sleep onset. Sensitivity analyses tightened mean-glucose calipers from 10 to 2 mg/dL.…

items.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Teacher Evolution
items.summary: On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), which aligns a student model's token-level distribution with that of its self-teacher prompted by privileged context, has emerged as a promising direction to mitigate reward sparsity in sequence-level post-training paradigms. However, OPSD often fails to achieve continuous performance gains during training. In this paper, we find that the model's limited self-teaching capability underlies this phenomenon by generating unreliable guidance on certain samples. To address this problem, we propose Teacher-Evolution Self-Distillation (TESD), which enables the self-teacher to generate rollouts and receive environmental feedback based on task correctness and context independence. First, using these rewards as training objectives, we perform teacher-oriented optimization to continuously enhance the model's self-teaching capability during distillation.…
items.tldr: Teacher-Evolution Self-Distillation improves on-policy self-distillation by continuously enhancing self-teaching reliability through reward-guided teacher optimization and adaptive down-weighting of unreliable samples.

items.title: Cross-Primitive Consistency in Jev
items.summary: Jev enables efficient decision-making with large language models (LLMs) through typed querying primitives, allowing the same semantic state to be expressed in different formats, such as binary and multiple-choice queries. However, the consistency of decisions across primitives has not been systematically evaluated. This work introduces PrimaCons, a four-axis benchmark for assessing cross-primitive consistency while preserving the semantics of the query. Evaluations across three Jev sizes reveal consistency violations across all four axes. Our analysis shows that these violations follow systematic patterns and that cross-primitive discrepancies predict decision failure with a ROC-AUC of 0.91.…
items.tldr: Jev's cross-primitive consistency is benchmarked and improved via a residual calibrator that reduces inconsistency and boosts decision accuracy.

items.title: A Tutorial on Generative Models for Music Audio
items.summary: Music audio generation spans instrumental clips, full songs with vocals, edits of existing recordings, and systems that play alongside a musician in real time. This monograph explains the methods behind these systems for readers familiar with neural-network training who are new to music generation. It introduces neural audio codecs and autoencoders, autoregressive and masked token models, diffusion and flow matching, sampling acceleration, and preference optimization in a shared notation. Worked examples connect training objectives and sampling procedures to published systems. The application sections relate the musical requirements of instrumental generation, songs, editing, and live performance to model design. Comparison tables record representations, methods, inputs, tasks, and release information documented in papers and official sources.…
items.tldr: This monograph surveys neural methods for music audio generation, covering codecs, autoregressive and diffusion models, flow matching, preference optimization, evaluation practices, and legal considerations.

items.title: Prompt Lottery in LLM-as-a-Judge: Measuring and Mitigating Sensitivity to Syntactic Rephrasing
items.summary: LLM-as-a-Judge has become a standard for evaluating large language models, yet most approaches implicitly assume that a single judge prompt functions as a stable evaluation instrument. Prior work has primarily explored deliberate prompt modifications such as scoring rubrics, role descriptions, or chain-of-thought reasoning in order to optimize accuracy. In contrast, we investigate whether validated prompt variants intended to preserve evaluation semantics while differing in surface realization (\textit{paraphrastic rephrasings}) yield consistent judgments under a fixed evaluation task. We introduce \textit{Prompt Lottery}, a phenomenon in which paraphrastic rephrasings produce different LLMaJ judgments.…

items.title: Vision Tomography: Towards Portable 3D Bidirectional Face-Skull Inference from Visual Data
items.summary: Traditional computed tomography (CT) can capture paired 3D face and skull geometry, but it remains costly, fixed in location, and exposes patients to radiation. For applications such as remote diagnostics, digital healthcare, forensic identification, missing-person investigation, and archaeological analysis, there is an urgent need for a portable, safe, and accessible solution to capture 3D skull geometry. In this work, we introduce Vision Tomography (VT), a concept and framework capable of reconstructing paired 3D face-skull geometry from various visual modalities, and also enabling joint manipulation of 3D facial and skull geometry. To achieve this, we first construct a dataset of over 200 samples, where each case includes a CT-based skull, a CT-based face, and a high-fidelity textured face scan.…
